3a0a5b6656388e8f: DORAL: For nearly two years, US President Donald Trump's heavy-handed deportation drive has sown fear in immigrant communities and generated a flood of grim headlines and social media videos.
Now, with midterm elections looming, many Latino voters who helped propel Trump and his Republican Party to power in 2024 say they are fed up.

In southern Florida's Doral, a mostly Latino community near Miami that is also home to one of Trump's golf clubs, residents told AFP that fears of potential raids have left businesses short-staffed and classrooms with fewer pupils.
Known as "Doralzuela", the area is home to a large Venezuelan population and could be a bellwether of shifting Latino sentiment nationwide.
"I feel sad and disappointed," restaurant owner Maria Fernanda Perez told AFP.
"My thinking was that the economy would improve," the 32-year-old said of her vote for Trump.
Three of her employees had stopped showing up for work for fear of being deported, she said, while sales had fallen 40 per cent as people in the community cut back on going out.
"My whole family, all my friends are going through immigration proceedings, and they're no longer working, they're no longer going about their daily lives."
Trump campaigned on promises of a historic deportation drive, but emphasised targeting hardened criminals.
With more than 1,000 people being taken into immigration custody every day, many Latino voters feel misled.
Like other communities around the country, residents in Doral have begun exchanging messages to alert one another to the presence of immigration agents or someone being detained.

A New York Times and Siena College poll conducted last month showed that 66 per cent of Hispanic respondents disapproved of Trump's performance, while 78 per cent said they would prefer Democrats to take control of Congress from Republicans.
Perez declined to say how she would vote in the upcoming election, but said emphatically: "Anyone but Trump."
Psychological pressure
Carlos Bermudez, a lawyer of Venezuelan origin, receives constant calls from desperate people going through immigration proceedings.
"They don't go out, they can't go to work... It's constant psychological pressure, and it affects the whole community," the 47-year-old told AFP.
Bermudez, who describes himself as a Republican, expressed concern about the party's increasingly "extreme" positions.

"I'm a Republican because I come from a country where communism, socialism took hold, and I don't want to continue with that ideology, but I don't agree with what the extreme wing of the party is doing now," he said.
Doral councilman Rafael Pineyro said he saw the crackdown's impact not only in his city but across southern Florida.
"There's uncertainty, there's fear... It's not just Doral, it's the whole Latino community in South Florida that's affected," he said from his office at city hall.
Pineyro, a Republican, also questioned the Trump administration's immigration strategy.
"This isn't right, because this isn't what was promised in 2024 when we were talking about (deporting) criminals," he said.
Trump's policies could undermine gains made by Republicans in recent years among Florida's Cuban, Venezuelan and other Latino voters, he warned.
"That opportunity has been slipping away more and more in recent months because of bad decisions, in my view, specifically when it comes to the economy and immigration."

2406e7b2a655fbb1: KUALA LUMPUR: Actor and comedian Datuk Afdlin Shauki Aksan was trapped in Paris for five hours amid riots, with his wife and three-year-old daughter.
In a Facebook post, Afdlin said he had travelled to France with his family to attend the International Market of Communications Programmes (Mipcom) in Cannes before spending time in Paris.
Their outing near the Louvre took a frightening turn when they encountered a demonstration.
"We came across a demonstration. Many of the participants were young people. To be fair, many of them were very polite and kind. Not everyone there was looking to cause trouble.
"When people began running in all directions, we were in front of a store. The staff saw us with Inaya, who is only three years old.
"They immediately let us in and locked the door," he said.
Afdlin said the family later left the store when the situation appeared to calm down, but could not find a way out of the area.
"Eventually, we took shelter in a restaurant connected to a nearby hotel."
He said he could not remember the restaurant's name but would always remember the elderly couple who ran it and the other patrons who looked out for his daughter.
Afdlin said the situation worsened when he saw rioters fleeing outside and tear gas seeped into the restaurant.
"My little girl began to panic and struggled to breathe. My wife was hit in the eyes by pepper spray, while I felt some tightness in my chest.
"As a father, seeing your own child frightened and struggling to breathe is incredibly difficult. At that moment, all we wanted was to make sure she was safe," he said.
Despite the ordeal, Afdlin cautioned against judging the whole of France based on incidents in one area.
"I heard reports of incidents elsewhere, including in Nice over the weekend, but I can only speak as a witness to what we experienced ourselves in Paris," he said.
He also urged Malaysians travelling abroad to prioritise their safety.
"Do not wait around to film or see what happens. Find shelter, follow the authorities' instructions and check official information before continuing your journey.
"No tourist attraction is more important than your family's safety. This experience left us frightened, but also deeply grateful," he said.

13f680a739dcd215: SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 21 — Netflix stock dropped more than 5 per cent yesterday afternoon after its quarterly earnings release failed to assuage investor concerns about a slowdown in viewer engagement and revenue growth.

“We know there’s some investor concern about our view hours growth,” the company said in a letter to investors, referring to how the company measures engagement, and added that it was “confident” it could accelerate that growth.
The California-based streaming giant has struggled to meet investor expectations for several quarters as it faces competition from other streamers, gaming and sports.

Netflix “has underperformed significantly over the last 6-12 months” and investors are concerned “about soft engagement trends, decelerating revenue growth, a slower margin expansion outlook, and most recently content executive leadership changes,” John Belton, a portfolio manager at Gabelli Funds, told AFP in a statement.
In its third quarter ending in September, Netflix recorded US$12.87 billion (RM52.51 billion) in revenue and US$3.7 billion in net income, above investor expectations, according to FactSet.
It did not provide overall figures for subscriber view hours in the quarter, but noted that in India the metric increased 24 per cent compared to the same period last year.
In July, Netflix said subscribers spent 97 billion hours watching content in the first half of the year, a 2 per cent increase over the first half of 2025.
It stopped reporting subscriber numbers in the first half of 2025.
But the company touted growth outside the US while acknowledging challenges stateside.

“We do need better execution in the US Our content around the world is largely working,” co-CEO Ted Sarandos told investors on an analyst call yesterday, highlighting engagement, subscribers, revenue and profits across Latin America, Europe and Asia.
“The US is also working. It’s just not growing as fast as it could or as fast as we’d like,” Sarandos continued.
Job cuts
The company will also reportedly cut around 6 per cent of its workforce, or 1,000 jobs, according to media reports.
Among them were seven high-level employees in charge of television deals and content, the Hollywood Reporter reported last week.

The company also recently replaced chief content officer Bela Bajaria, who oversaw popular shows including Stranger Things, Bridgerton, and Squid Game, in addition to pushing the company’s live entertainment strategy, according to CNBC.
Netflix appointed former Disney executive Peter Rice to be its new content chief.
“Peter Rice understands talent relations, and in a competitive market, creative talent have choices of where they want to work,” Sarandos said on the call yesterday.
Diverse formats
Competition from other streamers has forced Netflix to work harder to attract and retain both paid and ad-supported members.

The company has increasingly dipped into live sports — with agreements to stream major events like the Olympics and World Cup — in addition to gaming and shorter-form content. The NFL and WWE are also on board to stream live events.
In the US, it reached 7.8 per cent of streaming television viewers in July compared to YouTube’s 14.2 per cent, a record for the Google-owned site, according to media analytics firm Nielsen.
The World Cup lifted overall television viewership in July, according to Nielsen.

“It’s really important to remember, roughly 95 per cent of our spend and nearly all of our revenue is focused on that core, where we see a long runway for future growth,” Sarandos said on yesterday’s call, emphasising its commitment to traditional television and film content.
The company also missed expectations on advertising revenue growth.
“We are currently a bit behind our aggressive target for the year. We’re still growing” on advertising, nonetheless, co-CEO Greg Peters said on the call.
“We see the benefits when we continue to roll out other products like new ad formats, which help with our growth,” Peters added. — AFP
6fa5fe971d2d211c: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Police have dismantled a cross-border prostitution syndicate that used Malaysia as an offshore operational command centre to market sex workers to clients in Singapore, arresting one local and 29 foreign nationals in a coordinated bilateral blitz.

The joint crackdown, dubbed Op Noda – Rentas Sempadan, was mounted on Oct 20 by Bukit Aman’s Criminal Investigation Department (CID) alongside the Singapore Police Force (SPF) to stamp out networks managing online vice portals targeting Singaporean clientele.

“The success of this operation proves the effectiveness of the strategic synergy between the Royal Malaysia Police and the SPF through the sharing of intelligence, in achieving our common objective of curbing the activities of cross-border prostitution syndicates between both countries,” Bukit Aman CID director Datuk M. Kumarsaid in a statement today.

Equipped with intelligence on fugitives wanted across the Causeway, strike teams from Bukit Aman and the Johor contingent CID launched simultaneous raids on residential properties across Kuala Lumpur and Johor.

The opening wave of raids netted one Malaysian and eight foreign nationals, comprising five men and four women aged between 29 and 56. Checks on confiscated travel documents identified the foreign suspects as seven Chinese nationals and one Singaporean.

Investigators believe all nine operated as core members of a vice network wanted by the SPF under Section 146A(1)(b) of Singapore’s Women’s Charter 1961 and Section 109 of its Penal Code. Authorities also discovered that the Singaporean and four of the Chinese nationals were residing in Malaysia on expired visas.

Arrangements are underway to extradite the nine suspects to Singapore via Bukit Aman CID’s D12 division (Interpol/NCB) once their identities are confirmed before a magistrate under Section 5(3) of the Summons and Warrants (Special Provisions) Act 1971.

A concurrent phase of the operation netted another 21 foreign nationals, consisting of five men and 16 women aged 19 to 41, who are suspected of administering the syndicate’s online promotional machinery. The group includes 17 Chinese nationals, three Vietnamese, and one Laotian. Officers seized an array of electronic gadgets and communications gear allegedly used to field client queries and coordinate bookings.

The 21 suspects have been remanded under Section 117 of the Criminal Procedure Code. They face prosecution under Section 372(1)(e) of the Penal Code for exploiting individuals for prostitution through advertisements, an offence punishable by up to 15 years in prison, caning, and a fine.

They are also being investigated under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 for entering and remaining without a valid pass, which carries fines up to RM10,000, a maximum five-year jail term, and up to six strokes of the cane, alongside Section 15(1)(c) for overstaying.

Intelligence suggests the syndicate had operated in Singapore since 2024. By shifting its telecommunications hub and web hosting management to Malaysian residential hideouts, the syndicate sought to evade detection and complicate enforcement action by Singapore authorities.

Kumar warned that police will sustain “total enforcement” alongside local municipal authorities against all illicit vice networks, citing their destabilising toll on the economy and public welfare, and urged the community to continue tipping off law enforcement on cross-border syndicates.
91d14d88330acc40: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — The Housing and Local Government Ministry (KPKT) allocated RM154 million to local authorities (PBT) nationwide from 2023 to 2025 for the maintenance, repair and upgrading of public toilet facilities.
Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said the allocation had enabled 1,529 public toilets under the supervision of local authorities nationwide to be upgraded so far.

He said KPKT would continue these efforts by allocating a special RM30 million annually from 2026 to 2030, bringing the total allocation to RM150 million for the repair and upgrading of public toilets managed by local authorities over the next five years.

Meanwhile, Nga said cooperation between KPKT and the Education Ministry had also resulted in 11,835 school toilets nationwide being upgraded, which he described as the largest achievement of its kind in history.

He said providing public toilets that were clean, attractive and fragrant (BMW) was important to improving the people’s quality of life and reflecting the country’s level of civilisation and image, particularly as Malaysia sought to attract more foreign tourists.

“Public toilets are essentially the calling card at the forefront of a country’s image,” he said when delivering his speech at the Malaysia Best Toilet Awards 2026 (TOTYA’26), organised by KPKT, here tonight.

Also present were Deputy Housing and Local Government Minister Datuk Aiman Athirah Sabu, Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh, and Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Marhamah Rosli.

Nga said Malaysia was expected to receive 47 million foreign tourists this year, making the provision of clean and comfortable public toilet facilities an important aspect of supporting the country’s tourism sector.

He said awareness of the importance of public toilet cleanliness had also shown positive growth, with participation in TOTYA’26 increasing to 849 entries this year from 345 in its inaugural year, representing an increase of more than 200 per cent.

Now in its fourth edition, TOTYA’26 features eight categories: schools, places of worship, shopping centres, petrol stations, hotels, restaurants, local authorities, and toilets at rest and recreation (R&R) areas.

Among the winners of TOTYA’26 were Masjid Nurussalam in Gerik, Perak, in the places of worship category; Shah Alam City Council, for the public toilet at Tasik Barat, Section 14, Shah Alam, in the local authorities category; Iconic Marjorie Penang, a Tribute Portfolio Hotel in Bayan Lepas, in the hotel category; and Mamakim Wellness Kitchen Sdn Bhd in Desa Sri Hartamas, in the restaurant category.

Other winners were Sekolah Kebangsaan Tok Randok in Ajil, Hulu Terengganu, in the school category; Petronas Presint 18 in Putrajaya, in the petrol station category; Sunway Square Mall in Subang, in the shopping centre category; and the southbound Seremban Rest and Recreation (R&R) area along the North-South Expressway, operated by PLUS Malaysia Berhad, in the R&R category.
The winner in each category received RM20,000 in cash, a trophy and a certificate of recognition.

In addition, Nga said KPKT would introduce a new category at next year’s TOTYA for the Best Toilet at institutions of higher learning, universities and colleges, to encourage more educational institutions to prioritise toilet cleanliness and maintenance. — Bernama
ca9316d9ce3d9180: SOUTH AFRICA: Australia quick Mitchell Starc claimed his 450th test wicket on Tuesday but South Africa's lower order exposed the tourists' decision to omit spinner Nathan Lyon on day three of the second test.
Starc became only the 10th bowler to reach the milestone when Wiaan Mulder gloved a rising delivery from the 36-year-old to Matt Renshaw as South Africa slipped to 110-6.
The home side then turned the tables, seeing off the all-seam attack and the back-up part-timers and making the absence of Lyon more pronounced as they went on to score 425-9 before declaring.
It did not help that Josh Hazlewood, who took a career-best 6-49 in helping Australia to an emphatic 214-run victory in last week's first test, could only bowl after lunch.
He was sick on Monday, which meant he had to serve his time in the field on Tuesday before being allowed to bowl.
He made little impact in nine overs, however, while captain Pat Cummins went wicketless and Starc finished with 3-89.

Scott Boland, who replaced Lyon in the team, took his first five-wicket haul outside of Australia, but the tourists had to use Beau Webster to hold up an end and also turned to three other part-time spinners as South Africa piled on the runs.
Lyon would have arguably done a better job of stemming South Africa's free scoring on a day when captain Temba Bavuma notched a career-best 179 to give the hosts the upper hand.
"If you know you're going to be a man down from the start, you're probably going with a different make-up, aren't you?" Starc said.
"But unfortunately Josh had a dodgy prawn or something. He'll have fresh legs for the second innings."
Lyon was left to play a supporting role from the sidelines.
"He's been around long enough to put his shoes back on and be the team man that he is.
"He was that man for most of the day today, whether it's down at fine leg running us drinks or tapping us on the back.
"I've been left out plenty of times and naturally you're disappointed that you don't get to play. He'll get another opportunity," added Starc.
2570eacc1d73872b: SHAH ALAM, Oct 21 — The Selangor Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) has successfully uncovered the misappropriation of subsidised controlled goods specifically one-kilogramme (kg) packets of cooking oil following a raid on a premises in the Port Klang area, with the seized items valued at RM133,950.

Selangor KPDN director Muhamad Hanif Asa’ari said the suspected modus operandi involved bringing the packets of cooking oil to the premises, where they were mixed with used cooking oil in a dedicated storage tank.
He added that this mixture was allegedly kept for resale to companies that process used cooking oil, or distributed via the black market, in order to generate excessive profits.

“This activity is also believed to involve supplies sourced from parties suspected of holding valid licenses for scheduled controlled goods (CSA). The raid uncovered a large quantity of boxes containing packeted cooking oil, as well as plastic packets that had already been cut open.
“Approximately 15,900 kg of cooking oil, along with various equipment used in this operation including a lorry have been seized for further investigation,” he said yesterday.

Muhamad Hanif stated that the raid was conducted under the integrated ‘Ops Tiris 4.0’ which also involved the Marine Police and resulted in the detention of a foreign national in his 30s, who was employed at the premises, to assist with the investigation.

He added that the case is being investigated under the Control of Supplies Act 1961 [Act 122] and the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (AMLATFPUAA 2001) [Act 613].

“The Selangor KPDN will not compromise with any party found to be involved in such syndicates or illicit activities. We will continue to intensify monitoring and enforcement efforts to ensure that no one exploits or misappropriates subsidised controlled goods intended for the public,” he said. — Bernama
887971bf647a23f7: NEW YORK, Oct 21 — Wall Street stocks mostly rose yesterday, greeting a pullback in oil prices as investors steered funds towards industrial equities amid lingering caution over artificial intelligence shares.

Comments from Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesman Majed al-Ansari describing US-Iran talks as “ongoing” pressured crude prices, despite no concrete changes in a conflict that has dented energy supplies for more than seven months.
Saudi Arabia on Monday postponed a major investment conference due to repeated attacks from Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis.
International benchmark Brent oil futures finished down 0.7 per cent at US$108.79 (RM443.86) a barrel after earlier hitting US$111.99 a barrel.

Wall Street stocks began meekly following losing sessions in leading European and Asian markets. But US equities picked up momentum as the day progressed, especially the blue-chip Dow index led by strong results from industrial company 3M.
A more than one per cent rise in the Dow showed a “rotation” from tech shares, said Briefing.com analyst Patrick O’Hare.
“We still have some lingering softness in the tech trade and specifically the AI space so we’re not getting a completely broad market rally,” O’Hare said.
“But a lot of stocks outside the tech sector are doing reasonably well today with oil prices having come down and entry trades remaining relatively well behaved.”
Tech shares have lately been volatile, with analysts pointing to worries over AI profitability and the hefty debt financing of some companies.
The sector is also vulnerable after having outperformed the market for much of 2026.

“There’s some nervousness that perhaps the growth rates won’t be as strong as people have assumed which is to say you could have really good news but it just might not be good enough to satisfy high expectations,” O’Hare said.
Earlier, AI worries hit Asian exchanges.

Seoul and Tokyo again bore the brunt of the selling as chip giants SK hynix, Samsung and Kioxia took another beating owing to a sharp exit from a sector that saw blistering gains in the first half of this year.
South Korea’s Kospi stocks index sank nearly four per cent, with SK hynix off 4.2 per cent and Samsung down three per cent.
Further weighing on sentiment was the data center infrastructure firm Elice, whose shares collapsed more than 30 per cent on their trading debut.
The negative sentiment carried over to equity trading in Europe.
The euro rose against the dollar but remained under pressure as violent protests in France and Italy have pushed up government bond yields.

The yield on France’s 10-year government bond rose to 4.94 per cent yesterday, more than 150 basis points above the comparable German government bond, considered the European benchmark of creditworthiness.
The resulting spread between the two yields reached the greatest level since 2011.

Among individual companies, General Motors slumped 6.8 per cent despite reporting better profits than expected. However, the automaker pointed to a recent uptick in commodity costs due to the US-Iran war, clouding its profit outlook. — AFP
f2f835c81a06e7e8: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — When Saindhavi Srivatsan was five years old, she cried and insisted on holding a microphone to sing a devotional song (bhajan) at a temple.
Amused by her antics, the devotees obliged.
Little did they know then that the adamant little girl would grow up to become one of India’s most prominent female singers.
With nearly 3,000 songs in a career spanning more than two decades — more than half of them in Tamil — Saindhavi’s voice is widely cherished in Malaysia, a country she has visited more than 15 times.
In fact, she has even acquired the taste for a local favourite: milo dinosaur.
However, her recent trip here was to mark a 21-year career milestone, which she celebrated with her fans during the Up-Close & Personal with Saindhavi concert at Jiospace last Sunday.
The usually reserved singer opened up about her personal journey as a singer and some notable moments in her career.
“I never had a second career choice. Whenever my teachers asked me about my ambition, the answer was always the same: to be a singer,” she said.
One particular song, Kayilae Aagasam, is a song that she holds close to her heart.
“The song was recorded in my house, and I sat and sang the whole song because I was just days away from my delivering my baby,” she recalled.

A night to remember
For nearly four hours, she rendered her most iconic hits like Pirai Thedum, Yaaro Ivan and her award-winning song Ellu Vaya Pookalaye that left fans in both awe and tears.
She even infused contemporary flavours to some of her favourite classical devotional songs like Enna Thavam Seithanai and Deena Karunakarane Nadaraja, backed by a live band.
Local talents from reality singing shows organised by Astro like Theeban Mahendran and Siddarth Nagarajan also joined Saindhavi to serenade the fans.

Although Saindhavi’s name is synonymous with soulful melodies, she did not leave a dull moment for her fans and got them grooving to some of her peppy dance numbers and folk beats like Andangkaka Kondakari and Maduraikku Pogathadi.
Dancing live, she said, was something she deliberately avoided in her early years as a singer.
“I used to think people would not take me seriously as a singer if I dance while singing.
“But, nowadays, we are required to be performers. The love from my fans inspired courage in me to start dancing while singing,” she said.
The versatile Saindhavi also obliged to song requests from her audience and spontaneously performed Telugu and Malayalam songs as well during the show.

Tributes to legends

Prior to official debut as a playback singer, Saindhavi scored her first chance to enter the industry with the legendary music composer Devanesan Chokkalingam, fondly known as Thenisai Thendral Deva to his fans.
“I was in my 10th standard at that time. Deva sir did not dismiss me as just a child but gave me my first song but it never got released,” she said, recalling her memories with the maestro.
Deva passed away on October 17 at the age of 75 following a cardiac arrest.
Saindhavi performed an impromptu tribute to the maestro, stringing together a medley of his evergreen melodies such as Nalam Nalariyaval, Mudhal Mudhalil Parthen and Sakalakalavalavane.
“He always felt people boxed him into the ‘Gana’ label and on many occasions, he kept reiterating that he too has composed some beautiful melodies,” she said.
Saindhavi also offered a similar tribute for legendary female singers who have passed on such as Vani Jairam, Swarnalatha, Asha Bhosle and S. Janaki.
Both Asha Bhosle and S. Janaki also passed away this year at the age of 92 and 88, respectively.
Directed by Kumaran Ramasamy, the Up-Close and Personal with Saindhavi show will premiere on Astro Vinmeen (Ch 202) on November 9 at 10.30am.
463782d3636601c9: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — The Parliamentary Special Select Committee on Health (JKPK) will submit a memorandum regarding the cross-border haze issue to the Indonesian Embassy today.

Its chairman, Suhaizan Kaiat (PH-Pulai), said that the haze issue poses problems for the country across various aspects, such as the environment, public health, citizen safety, the national economy, and diplomatic relations between neighbouring countries.

"God willing, tomorrow morning the JKPK and its members will submit a memorandum to the Indonesian Embassy regarding this haze issue," he said while taking part in the debate on the Supply Bill (Budget) 2027 at the policy stage in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Meanwhile, Khoo Poay Tiong (PH-Kota Melaka) urged the government to take firm action against local companies allegedly involved in forest fires in Indonesia that caused the cross-border haze.

He said this follows a recent Greenpeace report naming 20 companies believed to be involved, including a leading national plantation company through its subsidiary registered in the neighbouring country.
"KLCC has now become 'KL Cannot See' because of the haze. In previous Special Chamber debates, the ministry informed that there was no information regarding the involvement of local companies.
"However, through this Greenpeace report, it is proven that there are local subsidiaries involved. We hope the ministry will not sit idly by and will take serious follow-up steps," he said.

Therefore, Khoo suggested that Malaysia follow the firm action of the Singaporean government in issuing warning notices to 10 companies believed to have links to the forest fire incidents in Indonesia.

Vivian Wong Shir Yee (PH-Sandakan) urged the government to provide a specific allocation for the long-term implementation of the Trap-Neuter-Release (TNR) method to address the stray animal issue nationwide, thereby breaking the cycle of conflict between the public, local authorities (PBT), and animal lovers following capture operations.

"When we lack a long-term system, every capture operation risks becoming a conflict, whether between animal lovers and the authorities or neighbour against neighbour. In the end, no one wins. Animals suffer, personnel are criticised, and public trust is eroded," she said.
According to Wong, a continuous TNR programme can gradually and ethically reduce the stray animal population without having to wait for tragedies to repeat.

The issue of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) was also raised during the debate, with Rodiyah Sapiee (GPS-Batang Sadong) asking the government to provide comprehensive insurance protection, including death and permanent disability compensation, as well as the welfare of health personnel involved in the FDS.

"I welcome the increase in the FDS health service incentive from RM30 to RM100. However, taking into account the risks faced by health personnel in the interior as well as lessons learned from the recent FDS helicopter crash incident, the government must ensure comprehensive protection," she said.

Datuk Andi Muhammad Suryady Bandy (BN-Kalabakan) raised the issue that 36 per cent, or 382 out of 1,055 medical officers offered permanent placements in Sabah and Sarawak this year, failed to report for duty, and suggested that the government review the Regional Incentive Payment (BIW) rate, which is currently set at RM360 per month.
"The BIW should be reverted to a percentage-based calculation system of salary as before, or a reasonable minimum rate set for officers serving in the interior of Sabah and Sarawak.
"Additionally, a special quota of 30 percent for students from Sabah and Sarawak in medical fields at public universities should be established," he said.
The Dewan Rakyat sitting continues tomorrow. — Bernama
06c596a74cd6ffcc: NEW YORK, Oct 21 — US officials gave final approval yesterday to the Boeing 737 MAX 10, certifying the latest long-delayed version of the popular single-aisle aircraft.

The Federal Aviation Administration issued a certificate confirming the largest plane in the MAX family “complies with all applicable design and safety requirements,” a Department of Transportation press release said.

The move, which follows US certification of the 737 MAX 7 in August, clears the way for increased plane deliveries in the coming years, a key aspect of Boeing’s plan to improve financial performance after a lengthy period of weakness.

“The FAA’s decision follows a thorough review of the aircraft’s design and safety requirements,” said FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford. “We will continue to hold Boeing to the highest safety standards as the company begins production of the 737 MAX-10.”
Boeing, which expects to commence 737 MAX 10 deliveries in 2027, said it undertook more than 2,000 hours of flight testing and supplied tens of thousands of pages of documentation.

“Our flight test team ran a disciplined, methodical campaign to validate every system,” said Chris Payne, general manager for 737 airplane development programs. “That rigor gives us confidence as we move toward deliveries.”
Faster certifications ahead?
Boeing first launched the aircraft at the 2017 Paris Air Show. In 2018, Boeing said it aimed to have deliveries in 2020.
When the 737 MAX 10 had its first flight in June 2021, Boeing targeted 2023 for first deliveries.
US regulators have heavily scrutinised Boeing’s designs during certifications following a pair of MAX crashes in 2018 and 2019 that together claimed 346 lives.
The process was also slowed by a near-catastrophic January 2024 Alaska Airlines flight in which a fuselage panel blew out mid-flight.
In January, Boeing unveiled a new MAX production line in Everett, Washington, supplementing output for a plane that had previously been assembled exclusively in Renton, Washington.
Yesterday’s announcement came in parallel with an expected visit by US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy to Everett.
Duffy told broadcaster CNBC that the United States needs to become more efficient in certifying aircraft, saying that European regulators needed only half the time.
“Safety is paramount, but we have to certify aircraft more quickly if we’re going to still compete as Americans,” Duffy told the network.
“I feel very confident if we all come together and get a better process in place, we’ll be just as, or more safe, but also can certify aircraft far more quickly.”
The MAX 10 lists maximum seats of 230, compared with 172 for the MAX 7, with the MAX 8 and the MAX 9 between the two, according to Boeing’s website.

Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg said at a Wall Street conference in September that he expects to increase output of the 737 MAX to 52 per month in 2027 from the current monthly level, which the FAA has authorised at 47.

During the September 16 appearance, Ortberg had said he expected FAA certification “very soon,” while also emphasising the company’s efforts to reach a deal with Boeing’s white-collar union that would avoid a strike.
FAA officials had in late September briefly paused certification over concerns about a software problem, but they later concluded the issue did not pose safety risks.
Boeing’s Society of Professional Engineering Employees in Aerospace approved a new contract on October 1, removing a potential strike from the list of Boeing concerns.
Shares of Boeing finished down 0.5 per cent. — AFP

b30aa642236fad6f: IN today's fast-paced digital landscape, a short video can inspire millions to pack their bags.
Recognising the power of social media to shape travel trends, Malaysia is leveraging global content creators to showcase its top attractions faster and more creatively.
The All Star Influencers Award (ASIA) 2026 brought together more than 100 content creators from 20 countries for a seven-month tourism campaign nationwide.

With a combined audience in the hundreds of millions across platforms like Instagram and TikTok, the project aims to boost the nation's culture, heritage, food, and local experiences during Visit Malaysia 2026 (VM2026).

ASIA chief executive officer Datuk Abd Rahman Soltan explained that the initiative has grown from a simple annual awards ceremony into a major global hub connecting tourism, digital media, cultural exchange, and creative industries.

"ASIA 2026 comes with a much bigger and more comprehensive vision. We want to make this platform a bridge connecting the digital world with the tourism sector more effectively and with greater impact," he said.

"Social media influence today plays a major role in shaping global travel trends. That is why we have brought together more than 100 influencers from different countries to ensure Malaysia receives extensive organic exposure throughout the programme."
Supported by the Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry (Motac) and Tourism Malaysia, the campaign saw influencers visit iconic landmarks, heritage sites, and lesser-known gems across 10 states.
Creators took part in community projects, media tours, and digital collaborations, sharing authentic personal stories rather than standard travel advertisements.
Beyond promoting tourism, ASIA helps creators build long-term business careers through its Influencer Partnership Programme (IPP).
Launched in 2025, the scheme matches creators with established businesses to design and release their own product lines.
"Many of these young influencers are talented, but they may not have business opportunities, capital or enough support to become 'celeb-preneurs'," Abd Rahman said.
The campaign's digital impact is staggering. Having recorded 205 million views in 2023, ASIA reached over 1.6 billion views in 2025, with four-year total views topping 3.8 billion.
The ASIA 2026 campaign wrapped up with a grand finale in Petaling Jaya, Selangor.
The top prize went to 31-year-old Indonesian creator Dinda Anwar, who was named Best Asia All Star 2026 during her very first time entering the programme.
She took home a trophy and US$10,000, along with the Best Culture Curator category award.
"I never expected this. I am so happy to win this title," said Dinda, reflecting on her six-day trip through Terengganu and Pahang.
"There are so many content creators today, so we have to produce something more special. This platform allows people to get to know Malaysia."
Pakistan's Zulqarnain took second place, winning US$5,000, while Vietnam's Duc Koi finished third, taking home US$3,000.
Ultimately, ASIA 2026 rests on a simple idea: when creators share genuine experiences, they connect in ways traditional ads cannot match — turning online views into real-life visits.

7483a1063602e280: OSLO, Oct 21 — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and the United States hailed “very productive” talks in Oslo yesterday amid efforts to draw a line under a bitter feud between Kyiv’s leader and US President Donald Trump over the war with Russia.
After talks with Trump’s envoys in the Norwegian capital, Zelensky thanked Washington for the resumption of US intelligence of looming Russian strikes on civilian targets and energy plants.
Trump’s special envoy Steve Witkoff is now due to head from Oslo to Russia for talks with President Vladimir Putin today in a bid to end Russia’s four-year-old war on Ukraine.

The positive tone followed days of tensions between Kyiv and Washington since Trump struck a diesel-supply deal with Putin, and furiously called for Zelensky to be replaced after Ukraine refused to stop hitting Russian oil refineries.

“We are thankful that intelligence works,” Zelensky told reporters in Oslo. “I’m speaking about early warning, what is very important for our people, for children, adults, civilians, because we can hear when ballistic is coming.”
Flanked by Norway’s Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store and Finnish President Alexander Stubb — a golfing buddy of Trump — Zelensky said it was “important that we keep the conversation going.”

A US official told AFP after the talks that Zelensky held “very productive and constructive discussions” with businessman Witkoff and Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, who took part remotely due to the flu.
“Ukraine brought forward new ideas and proposals,” the official said.
‘Make a deal’
But Trump kept up the pressure, saying at the White House that he wanted Zelensky to “make a deal” with Russia, which is escalating strikes on Ukraine as a bitter winter looms.
Trump, who last week called on Zelensky to resign, also criticized Zelensky for not accepting the terms he said he had offered during their infamous televised row in the Oval Office in February 2025.
Relations plunged back into a deep freeze earlier this month after Trump suddenly announced his deal with Russia for diesel, as part of his efforts to lower oil prices sent soaring by his Iran war.
Ukraine reacted with dismay after Trump also waived sanctions against Russia’s war machine and appeared to once again pivot to Putin.

The feud spiraled as Zelensky accused Trump of weakness, and then alleged that the United States was deliberately withholding vital intelligence and delaying the delivery of vital interceptor missiles.
Ukraine has also reported a reduction in speeds on Starshield, the US military satellite system which it uses for battlefield communications and strikes on Russian-occupied territory.
Trump has denied ordering a reduction in speeds on Starshield after Musk — whose company SpaceX developed it — said the order could only have come from the White House.
But the Wall Street Journal reported yesterday that it was indeed Musk who ordered the slowdown in the military-grade version of Starlink.
‘Our future’
The Oslo meeting followed furious diplomatic efforts in Washington, Kyiv and Western capitals to calm the situation.
Zelensky said earlier yesterday he had held “substantive” talks with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

Zelensky separately told US senators on Monday that “the Pentagon is delaying the delivery of missiles” already paid for by European countries, and that the shipment was waiting for US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth’s signature.
Several European countries were ready to transfer Patriot interceptor missiles from their own stockpiles but were still awaiting US approval, he said.
Trump — whose Republican party faces tough midterm elections amid dismal polling and high fuel prices — has accused Zelensky of not trying to resolve the conflict with Russia.

Trump said he was ready to meet Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in China next month to discuss denuclearisation, adding that talks could also cover the Ukraine war — fuelling fears in Kyiv that it was being sidelined.
Zelensky insisted yesterday that Kyiv needed to be represented at any meeting regarding Ukraine’s future.
“If there are issues about Ukraine, our future, it can be acceptable only when we are at the table of negotiations. It’s absolutely clear,” he said. — AFP

c2a06ae4e0b282c4: EDMONTON, Oct 21 — Separatists in Canada’s Alberta province say their independence fight is not over despite a decisive referendum loss, risking long-term political turmoil in an oil-rich province crucial to the Canadian economy.
The western province chose overwhelmingly on Monday to remain a part of Canada, with 75.5 per cent of voters rejecting a plan to move forward with a binding independence referendum.
As he entered parliament yesterday, Prime Minister Mark Carney said he was “thrilled that Albertans have chosen unity.”

Asked what message he’d like to deliver to the separatist side, Carney, who grew up in Alberta, said: “The result is absolutely clear. It’s a large majority for Canada and now is the time to work together.”
But separatist leaders projected a starkly different message after the results came in.
Jeffrey Rath, a top official with the Alberta Prosperity Project who met with US officials earlier this year to discuss support for the secession project, said the fight would “absolutely” continue.
“We’ve created a massive movement in this province,” he said. “We’re continuing to move forward.”
Rath told reporters it was impossible to win an independence referendum while Alberta is led by someone who supports Canadian unity.
He vowed to challenge Premier Danielle Smith, who aligned with Carney, and “to take control back” of Alberta’s conservative movement.
“We will form a government, period,” he said.
‘Deep-seated grievances’
Alberta’s separatist movement is factionalised.
Chris Scott, who founded Let’s Talk Alberta to promote independence, told AFP yesterday that he will also continue pushing the cause.
But, he said, plans for separatists to immediately take over the provincial government and launch another referendum would fail.

“Seventy-five per cent of Albertans would reject that idea flat out,” he said. “People have to realise you can gain some support for an idea or a movement by sharing Facebook memes, but at a certain point you have to focus on the real work of education.”
For Carney, Alberta is essential to his plans to solidify Canada’s economy and reduce dependence on the United States.
He and Smith are working together on advancing a new pipeline from Alberta to the Pacific coast, hoping to export Alberta bitumen to Asia.
Experts warned that despite Carney’s message of unity, there may be trouble ahead.
The referendum result was not enough to “completely close debate” on secession, University of Ottawa political scientist Geneviève Tellier told AFP.
“We can no longer trivialise this movement,” she added.
Tellier said Carney handled the separatist push well and massive federal financial support for a pipeline was an effective way to contain secessionist momentum.
But, she argued, the moment that federal money for major Alberta projects runs out, “problems are likely to start for Mr. Carney.”
Writing in yesterday’s Globe and Mail, Alberta expert Tyler Dawson warned that “there are deep-seated grievances in this province, and a ‘remain’ vote does not make those issues go away.”
Resentments persist on several issues, including perceptions that the provincial oil industry is being suppressed by environmental regulations.
“Roughly one-quarter of Albertans have said they want to hold another referendum on leaving Canada. Mr Carney mustn’t discount that,” Dawson said. — AFP
dc40f0336b596236: KUALA LUMPUR: Iskandar Malaysia has attracted RM525.26 billion in investments over two decades, exceeding its original RM383 billion target by RM142.26 billion, as Johor's flagship economic corridor shifts towards higher-value industries and deeper cross-border integration to sustain its next phase of growth.

The focus is now on translating investment momentum into higher productivity, better-paying jobs and stronger domestic supply chains, with the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) expected to play a pivotal role in positioning the region as a more competitive regional business and industrial hub.
According to the Iskandar Regional Development Authority (IRDA), the corridor has generated more than one million jobs and more than doubled average household incomes since its establishment.

With competition for investments intensifying across Asean, IRDA is shifting its priorities from broad-based expansion towards quality investments that deliver greater economic value, strengthen local businesses and create opportunities for Malaysians to move up the value chain.

The next phase will prioritise advanced manufacturing, digital and data-driven industries, modern logistics, and high-value financial and business services, positioning Iskandar Malaysia to capture a greater share of regional and global economic activity.

"For the next development phase, emphasis will be placed on increasing productivity and high-value economic activity, including advanced manufacturing, digital and data-driven industries, and logistics, as well as financial and business services," IRDA said in a statement.

The authority said the emphasis would extend beyond the value of investments secured to include technology transfer, domestic business participation, local innovation and the ability of Malaysian companies to move up the global value chain.

At the centre of this strategy is the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ), which is expected to strengthen the economic relationship between the two markets by combining Johor's industrial capacity and competitive operating expenses with Singapore's access to international capital, technology and business networks.

The JS-SEZ attracted RM76.98 billion in approved investments in 2025, underscoring Johor's growing appeal as a complementary investment destination for businesses seeking to expand their regional operations.

Deputy Prime Minister II and Energy Transition and Water Transformation Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said the next phase of Iskandar Malaysia's development must be measured by the quality and sustainability of its economic gains, rather than investment figures alone.
Fadillah chaired the 36th IRDA Governing Council meeting on behalf of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, alongside Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi.

"The next phase should be assessed not only by the total investment attracted but also by the quality of opportunities created, the strength of the economic ecosystem, and the long-term benefits that businesses and communities can enjoy," he said.

IRDA said land availability and competitive costs, once major considerations for investors, were no longer sufficient to secure a competitive advantage as businesses increasingly assessed the readiness of infrastructure, reliability of energy supply, availability of skilled workers and quality of digital connectivity.
The efficiency of cross-border movement for goods and people, as well as access to regional and international markets, has also become increasingly important in investment decisions.
In this regard, the JS-SEZ offers an opportunity to create a more integrated economic ecosystem by leveraging the complementary strengths of Johor and Singapore.

"Johor has the opportunity to combine advantages in land, industrial capacity, talent, and cost with Singapore's strengths in capital, technology, business services, and access to international markets.

"However, realising the JS-SEZ potential requires alignment in infrastructure development, energy supply, talent development, customs and immigration processes, and cross-border connectivity," IRDA said.

Olive Tree Property Consultants founder and chief executive officer Samuel Tan said the corridor's next phase would depend on how effectively these complementary advantages could be translated into tangible business benefits.

He said investors were increasingly looking beyond low operating expenses and land availability, with infrastructure readiness, dependable energy supply, access to skilled talent and seamless connectivity becoming critical factors in determining where companies establish or expand their operations.

"The JS-SEZ creates a significant advantage by bringing together complementary strengths that no single jurisdiction could offer in isolation. This includes Johor's abundant land, established industrial capacity, growing talent pool and competitive operating expenses, alongside Singapore's global capital networks, technology, business services and access to international markets," he told Business Times.

However, Tan said the zone's long-term competitiveness would depend on effective coordination between the two jurisdictions, particularly in infrastructure planning, energy security, workforce development and the movement of goods and people across the border.

Streamlining customs and immigration procedures and strengthening physical and digital connectivity would also be essential to improving operational efficiency for businesses operating across both markets.

For Iskandar Malaysia, the challenge is to convert its investment momentum into a more sophisticated economic base that delivers sustained productivity gains, higher-value jobs and greater participation by domestic companies.

The success of the JS-SEZ will therefore be measured not only by its ability to attract more capital but also by how effectively it integrates businesses, develops local talent and strengthens Johor's position in regional and global supply chains.

3e6a60d4905581f0: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Haze continued to blanket much of the peninsula this morning, with 22 of the country’s 68 monitoring stations in the unhealthy range, according to the Department of Environment (DOE).

As of 8am, the DOE dashboard showed 22 stations with Air Pollutant Index (API) readings of 101 to 200. Another 39 stations were in the moderate range and seven were in the good range. No station recorded very unhealthy or hazardous levels.
The unhealthy count is down from 25 at 4pm yesterday, when 35 stations were moderate and eight were good.

Bukit Rambai in Melaka recorded the highest reading at 174, up from 166 yesterday afternoon. It displaced Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur, which topped yesterday’s list at 173 but has since eased to 159. Bandaraya Melaka rose to 162 from 156, and Alor Gajah to 158 from 156, so all three Melaka stations remain unhealthy.
Negeri Sembilan’s readings were broadly steady. Nilai recorded 161, down from 165, Seremban 158, down from 161, and Port Dickson 155, up slightly from 154.

In Selangor, Johan Setia, near a peat fire hotspot, recorded 160, down from 171 yesterday. Klang and Banting were both at 159, Shah Alam at 158 and Petaling Jaya at 157, all lower than yesterday afternoon. In Kuala Lumpur, Cheras eased to 159 from 169, while Putrajaya recorded 158, down from 164.

Johor had seven unhealthy stations. Batu Pahat recorded 157, up from 153, and Larkin 155, down from 159. Tangkak stood at 153, Pasir Gudang at 152 and Kluang at 151. Segamat recorded 123, and Kota Tinggi fell sharply to 111 from 155 yesterday, the lowest reading on this morning’s unhealthy list. Pengerang, which was at 155 yesterday afternoon, is no longer in the unhealthy range.

Paka in Terengganu was the only station outside the west coast and Johor still unhealthy, at 153. The three Perak stations unhealthy yesterday, Tasek Ipoh, Pegoh Ipoh and Tanjung Malim, have dropped off the list.

Haze has persisted despite recent rainfall, which offered only temporary relief while fresh smoke continued to drift in from forest fires in Indonesia. Veterinarians have also reported pets suffering respiratory problems, including asthma attacks in cats and dogs needing oxygen therapy.
Authorities have previously advised high-risk groups and people with respiratory conditions to wear masks outdoors and to monitor hourly API updates on official DOE channels.

790030a71c46424e: PARIS, Oct 21 — French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu yesterday vowed a “massive” police presence at fresh protests called for the coming weekend, as he faced criticism over the handling of recent street violence.

The eurozone’s second-largest economy was rocked on Saturday by some of its worst rioting in recent years, just six months before voters head to the polls to elect a successor to President Emmanuel Macron.
Facing angry lawmakers in parliament, Lecornu acknowledged that the security response had fallen short and promised a stronger approach ahead of a new wave of protests.
“The deployment for next Saturday will be massive,” Lecornu said.
He accused ultra-left radical groups of forging an “insurrectionary plan” that led to the riots, which erupted on the sidelines of nationwide protests over the cost of living.

Images of clashes, mobs looting stores and public buildings set ablaze last weekend prompted several countries, including the United States, China and Germany, to issue travel advisories for their citizens in France.
French authorities on Monday announced partial curfews in Paris and some other cities, and Lecornu said fresh curfews would be imposed yesterday where needed.

The nighttime curfew in the capital, from 2100 GMT yesterday, applied to Republique square in the centre east and the Les Halles district in the centre that is full of shops. A ban on public gatherings was also ordered for the Champs-Elysees, near several public buildings, and at train stations.
Paris police also ordered a temporary ban on people carrying cans or bottles of petrol or gas, after mobs set fire to government buildings and shops last weekend.
‘War films’

During the night, a helicopter flew over the French capital’s Place de la Republique, one of the epicentres of the unrest, sweeping a searchlight across the square to monitor compliance with the curfew.
“The sound of a helicopter at one in the morning is a bit oppressive,” said Sylvain Courant, a resident of the Les Halles neighbourhood, another hotspot of the street violence.
“It’s that thing you see on TV, in all the good war films.”
Macron, currently on a Gulf tour where he secured additional diesel supplies in an effort to bring down prices, has acknowledged shortcomings in the handling of the protests.
France’s government is wrestling with high public debt and anger over soaring prices, and facing a strong challenge from the far right.
The unrest on Saturday broke out after around half a million people turned out across France to denounce the cost of living, following four weeks of school protests.
‘Wake-up call’
Security forces arrested a man believed to be connected to the ultra-left over the burning down of a historic town hall in Limoges, whose destruction has become a symbol of the violence.

Authorities have faced criticism from parties across the political spectrum, with far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen describing the unrest as a “wake-up call” that exposed a “profound crisis” of authority.
Recent polling suggests Le Pen leading first-round presidential voting intentions by a wide margin and far-left candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon emerging as the strongest contender for the runoff.

In a sign of growing political scrutiny over the street violence, lawmakers from across France’s fractured parliament agreed yesterday to launch a parliamentary inquiry into the unrest, including possible intelligence failures, policing tactics and the government’s preparedness.
Investors have sold off French debt in recent weeks amid rising doubts about the government’s ability to rein in spending.
Under pressure to support thousands of damaged or looted shops, the government said interest-free loans would be made available from Friday to all affected businesses, along with other measures.
Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said nearly 150 people had been jailed and more than 800 brought before the courts.
He argued that a strong judicial response was necessary to prevent ordinary people from taking matters into their own hands.
“The justice system is being extremely firm,” he said. “People with no previous criminal record are being sent to prison.”
Some demonstrators were seriously injured. One man lost a hand to a police grenade. In the eastern city of Mulhouse, a 17-year-old girl lost an eye.
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez offered to resign on Sunday, saying police “had lost control” during the unrest. Macron rejected his resignation.
Troops in Milan
Other European countries have also seen demonstrations over rising prices, with smaller clashes breaking out in Milan, Italy’s financial centre, and Belgium over the weekend.
Italy’s government yesterday announced the deployment of 500 troops to Milan until the end of the year to assist police.

US President Donald Trump has seized on the unrest in France to amplify his anti-immigration and anti-Islam rhetoric, at a time when his Republican party is facing strong headwinds in the upcoming midterm elections.
“It’s immigration, and I told President Emmanuel Macron, close up your borders,” said Trump.
Several analysts countered that immigration was not a driving force in France’s unrest. — AFP
331d7d7e0226a2f0: WANGARATTA, Oct 21 — The man alleged to have critically wounded Australian lawmaker Helen Haines in a “targeted” attack appeared in court today, as police warned that growing extremism online was fuelling political polarisation.

Haines is in “critical but stable condition” at a Melbourne hospital after being struck by a car on Monday near her office in the town of Wangaratta, more than 200 kilometres (124 miles) northeast of the Victoria state capital, police said today.
Local media reported that she had undergone surgery, losing one of her legs and is fighting to keep the other.

Police have charged 43-year-old Brendan Nugent with dangerous driving causing serious injury and intentionally causing serious injury, as well as the federal crime of harming a public official, which carries a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison.
He appeared at a courthouse in Wangaratta today, an AFP journalist at the scene said.
National broadcaster ABC said he had not applied for bail. His next hearing is scheduled for February 4.

The alleged attack has sparked soul-searching in a country where political violence is rare, but where police have documented a steady rise in threats and abuse directed towards elected officials in recent years.
The motive remains unknown and authorities have refused to speculate while the investigation takes place.
But police said today they were examining all possible leads, including that he may have held radical anti-government views.
“Like everyone, we’re examining social media associations, talking to witnesses, friends and colleagues,” Victoria police commissioner Mike Bush told journalists.
And Australian Federal Police (AFP) Commissioner Krissy Barrett said there is a growing level of “extremist views” online.

“The current criminal threat environment is febrile, and when it comes to federal parliamentarians, the AFP continues to record the growing volume of online abuse, threatening rhetoric, and intimidation,” she said.
‘World is more dangerous’
The independent lawmaker, 65, was standing near the trunk of her car when she was struck by a Toyota Land Cruiser on Monday afternoon.
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has led an outpouring of support for Haines, who was widely praised for her efforts to increase transparency in politics and crack down on corruption.
He bemoaned the fact that political debate in Australia had grown too heated and personal over the past few years.
“It’s a reminder that the world is a more dangerous and divided place than it was a generation ago,” Albanese told ABC Melbourne radio today.
“I think that Australians do want to see their politicians be able to go about their business, to be able to get something from the back of their car, for goodness sake,” he said.

Australia’s spy agency chief Mike Burgess warned following the alleged attack that “elevated levels of grievance, intolerance and polarisation continue to create a permissive environment of violence”.
Haines entered parliament in 2019 after working as a nurse and midwife, becoming known for stances such as supporting stronger climate action. — AFP
14cd5043dd4d762e: A CHILD'S future is full of possibilities. Many children start developing their ambitions and dreams young.

For parents, preparing for their children's future is not something that can be achieved overnight. It requires early planning and consistent effort, including setting aside savings for their education.

Through Bulan Menabung Simpan SSPN (BMS) 2026, the National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) is highlighting the importance of saving as a key step parents can take to prepare for their children's education future.

BMS 2026 runs from Sept 25 to Nov 1, with the theme "Under the Sea". The campaign likens the savings journey to exploring the depths of the ocean, where countless wonders and possibilities await discovery.
The deeper one dives, the more there is to discover. Similarly, a child's journey through life presents numerous opportunities and possibilities.
Some children dream of becoming doctors, teachers, engineers, entrepreneurs or athletes, while others aspire to pursue creative careers.
Each dream comes with its own journey and education is one of the key foundations that can help prepare children for the future.
Every contribution to a child's savings is a small but meaningful step towards helping them achieve their ambitions.
Parents do not need to wait until they have accumulated a substantial amount before they start saving. What matters most is taking the first step early and developing a consistent saving habit.
When it comes to shaping children's future, parents can become real-life superheroes, always standing behind them, offering support and providing for their needs.
Saving for education is not merely about setting aside money. It also reflects parents' love, commitment and determination to secure a better future for their children.
Although children may not yet understand the importance of savings, the efforts parents make from an early age can help prepare them for when they are ready to pursue further education.
Through the tagline "Jom Jadi Superhero Anak Anda!", BMS 2026 encourages parents to play their role in everyday life.

A superhero does not need to wear a costume or have extraordinary powers. To a child, a superhero can be a mother or father who is willing to plan ahead, make sacrifices and prepare for the future to give them the opportunity to pursue their dreams.
Preparing for a child's future can begin with one simple step today: saving.
Every contribution serves a purpose, every step carries meaning and every childhood dream deserves to be supported by careful preparation.

Through BMS 2026, parents are reminded that their children's future is not something they must wait to discover. Instead, they can begin exploring the possibilities today, one savings contribution at a time.
Parents are encouraged to take part in the BMS 2026 Closing Programme, which will be held from Oct 29 to Nov 1 at the Centre Court, Alamanda Shopping Mall, Putrajaya.
