3bdf0cfe649dda4d: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 21 — Clean-up works at Parit Cina and Sungai Kereh in Tasek Gelugor are expected to begin in the first quarter of 2027 to remove accumulated sediment, improve water flow and help reduce pollution in the area.

State Local Government and Town & Country Planning Committee chairman Jason H’ng Mooi Lye said the initiative was among the state government’s efforts to address the pollution of Sungai Kereh, an issue that has persisted for decades.

He said 61 pig farms are currently operating in Kampung Selamat, Tasek Gelugor, but the source of the pollution has to be identified based on evidence and on-site inspection findings, rather than drawing conclusions based on a single activity.

“The pollution issue in Kampung Selamat needs to be examined by taking into account various factors, including agricultural activities, waste management and discharge, drainage systems, and other environmental aspects that fall under the jurisdiction of various agencies.

“The state government’s priority for now is to ensure that the source of pollution in Sungai Kereh is identified through comprehensive inspections and assessments. Enforcement action will be taken against parties that violate regulations, and corrective measures will be implemented effectively,” he said in a statement today.

H’ng said the state government is also strengthening pig farm waste management through a short-term action plan involving the transportation of waste to biogas plants, and a long-term plan involving a proposal to construct a biogas plant facility in Kampung Selamat, as presented by the Penang Veterinary Services Department on May 11.
Under the short-term plan, he said solid and liquid waste from pig farms in Kampung Selamat is being transported to the biogas plant in Ampang Jajar.

For pig farms in Seberang Perai Tengah, the transportation of solid and liquid waste to the biogas plant in Kampung Valdor began in June 2026, while waste transportation from farms in Seberang Perai Selatan has commenced since 2023.
“These measures are aimed at strengthening livestock waste management through appropriate processing facilities and reducing the risk of waste discharge that could harm the environment.

“As for the long-term solution, a proposal to build a biogas plant facility in Kampung Selamat has also been put forward to enable livestock waste to be managed more systematically and sustainably,” he said.

H’ng said the pig farming industry has the potential to contribute to the state’s economic growth and support related sectors. However, this has to be balanced with operators’ responsibility to comply with regulations and ensure that farming activities do not adversely affect the environment or the well-being of the community.

Yesterday, Tasek Gelugor Member of Parliament Datuk Wan Saifulruddin Wan Jan proposed in the Dewan Rakyat that pig farming activities in Tasek Gelugor be halted following the pollution of Sungai Kereh, which has been linked to the discharge of untreated waste from nearby pig farms in Kampung Selamat. — Bernama
2c5683c6cb6ff9b4: LIVERPOOL, Oct 21 — Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola said the Reds cannot afford to relax after storming back from a two-goal deficit to beat Villarreal 4-3 yesterday and maintain a perfect start to their Champions League campaign.
Villarreal coach Inigo Perez looked set to get one over on his old boss Iraola as the Spaniards deservedly took a 2-0 lead inside 30 minutes through Georges Mikautadze and Sergi Cardona.
But twice the visitors were undone by their failure to defend crosses into the box as Alexis Mac Allister and Ronald Araujo levelled before half-time.

Mac Allister fired in his second 25 minutes from time and substitute Florian Wirtz completed the comeback as Liverpool moved alongside Paris Saint-Germain at the top of the Champions League table with nine points from three games.
“In the first half, especially the first 30-35 minutes, they have been much better than us. In the second half, especially the first 30-35 minutes, we were much better,” said Iraola.
“I think when we’ve been under pressure and we had to go and leave everything, I think we’ve answered well.
“When we’ve relaxed a little bit at the beginning of the game, or when you score the 4-2, you think, ‘ok it’s done’, it has cost us. You cannot relax.”

Iraola left out all three of his over £100 million (RM546 million) forwards as Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola joined Wirtz on the bench with one eye on the visit of high-flying Brighton in the Premier League on Sunday.
Villarreal took full advantage of the much-changed Liverpool side early on and were gifted the opening goal after just four minutes.
Virgil van Dijk miscued his attempted header back to Alisson Becker and Mikautadze finished coolly from close range.
Perez’s own managerial career got started by chance when he was denied a work permit to join Iraola as his assistant at Bournemouth.
Instead he ended up as boss at Rayo Vallecano, where he had previously worked under Iraola, and led the La Liga minnows to the Conference League final last season.
Ngumoha ‘the difference’
Perez’s knowledge of Iraola’s system was clear as Villarreal opened up Liverpool at will at times during the first half.
A fine team move finally led to a second goal when Nathan Saliba picked out the run of Cardona from left-back and he steered the ball past Alisson.
Liverpool’s understudies in attack had barely threatened until Mac Allister’s looping header from a Kostas Tsimikas corner kickstarted the fightback.
Rio Ngumoha then began to tease the Villarreal defence but the first of two assists for the 18-year-old owed a lot to poor defending.
Cardona let Ngumoha’s cross go at the back post, unaware that Araujo was steaming in to head in the equaliser.
That was the Uruguayan’s last act as he made way for Wirtz at half-time and Liverpool clicked through the gears after the break.
Ngumoha’s searing pace down the right wing opened up the Villarreal defence and his low cross was smashed in off the underside of the bar by Mac Allister.
“He was amazing tonight,” said Mac Allister on Ngumoha’s impact. “He made the difference.”
Just three minutes later Cody Gakpo picked out Wirtz to score his first goal of the season and hit back at his critics over a lack of end product.
Iraola’s men remained suspect at the back, though, and Tani Oluwaseyi set up a nervy finish with a sweet connection to Ayoze Perez’s cross.
But Liverpool held on to close in on the last 16 and leave Villarreal on just three points from their first three games. — AFP
2d875cf1a73c6945: KUALA LUMPUR: Twenty-two areas nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality as of 8am today.
According to the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), the affected areas were in Johor, Negri Sembilan, Kuala Lumpur, Melaka, Putrajaya, Selangor and Terengganu.
In Johor, the areas with unhealthy air quality readings were Batu Pahat (157), Larkin (155), Tangkak (153), Pasir Gudang (152), Kluang (151), Segamat (123) and Kota Tinggi (111).
In Negri Sembilan, the affected areas were Nilai (161), Seremban (158) and Port Dickson (155).
In Kuala Lumpur, Batu Muda and Cheras each recorded an API reading of 159, while Putrajaya recorded 158.
In Melaka, Bukit Rambai recorded an API reading of 174, followed by Bandaraya Melaka (162) and Alor Gajah (158).
In Selangor, Johan Setia recorded 160, followed by Klang and Banting (159), Shah Alam (158) and Petaling Jaya (157). In Terengganu, Paka recorded 153.
Meanwhile, APIMS data showed that 39 other air quality monitoring stations nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while seven areas recorded good air quality.
API readings of 0 to 50 are classified as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and readings above 300 as hazardous.
bb2d666cb6cc503d: MADRID: Real Madrid are seeking contributions towards the setup costs of the failed European Super League project from the six Premier League clubs that withdrew shortly after its launch, the Spanish side confirmed to Reuters on Tuesday.

The Athletic reported that the total costs could reach €80 million (US$89.9 million). Real are seeking payments from Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur.
The six were among nine of the competition's 12 founding clubs that withdrew within three days of its launch in 2021 amid widespread opposition.
Real did not immediately confirm whether they were also seeking payments from the other three early leavers, AC Milan, Inter Milan and Atletico Madrid.
Real Madrid said the six English clubs were liable for costs incurred in establishing the competition, which have so far been covered by Juventus, Barcelona and Real.
Tottenham declined to comment while the other five Premier League clubs did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

The Athletic reported that the clubs signed a shareholders' agreement for the European Super League Company, the holding company behind the competition, although it is unclear whether the contract explicitly set out their liability for setup costs.
The Super League collapsed shortly after its launch following the withdrawal of the nine clubs.
Juventus subsequently pulled out of the project and Barcelona formally withdrew in February, leaving Real Madrid as its sole remaining founding club.
Real, Uefa and European Football Clubs announced an agreement of principles on Feb 11 aimed at resolving their Super League-related legal disputes.
f62deaafcb8b74e8: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) has denied any involvement in the Registrar of Societies’ (RoS) decision to cancel the registration of Perikatan Nasional (PN) today.

PKR secretary-general Datuk Fuziah Salleh described as defamatory the allegation by Parti Pejuang Tanahair (Pejuang) president Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir that the decision was made on PKR’s recommendation.

She also refuted Mukhriz’s social media post featuring several slides purportedly detailing PKR’s plan to deregister PN, which he claimed had been presented at the party’s 2026 National Congress in Melaka last August.
“I consider the use of slides that were never presented, in an attempt to link PKR to the RoS decision on PN, to be defamatory.
“I therefore demand that Mukhriz retract the allegation and apologise to PKR. Political differences are no licence to spread defamatory allegations,” she said in a Facebook post.
Fuziah added that the complaint which prompted the RoS action against PN concerned issues involving the coalition’s own component parties, and PKR had absolutely no involvement in the matter.
In a statement today, RoS said it deregistered PN after finding that the explanation submitted by the coalition had failed to rebut the grounds for deregistration stated in an earlier notice.
RoS said it made the decision after examining all the documents and explanations submitted by PN on Oct 12.
It added that the reasons provided by PN also failed to offer sufficient justification for maintaining the coalition’s registration. — Bernama
c153cbf31fdde6eb: KOTA BARU: Perikatan Nasional secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan has challenged Bersatu Youth to substantiate its allegations against him and PN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar over the coalition's deregistration.
He said Bersatu Youth had the right to express its views but should provide evidence to support its claims instead of making allegations against the two leaders.
"We challenge him (Bersatu Youth information chief Harris Idaham Rashid) to prove his allegations.
"He has the right to say whatever he wants, but he should not make allegations against me and Samsuri.
"When both of us held positions in PN, there were no problems. PN even won several seats in the Johor and Negri Sembilan elections," he said.

Takiyuddin was speaking at the Ceramah Jelajah Himpunan dan Munajat Penyatuan Ummah (Himpak), held in conjunction with the 36th anniversary celebrations of Kelantan Membangun Bersama Islam in Pasir Tumboh last night.
Yesterday, Bersatu Youth blamed Takiyuddin and Samsuri for the coalition's deregistration by the Registrar of Societies Malaysia (RoS).
Harris has claimed that the crisis stemmed from failures to manage meeting procedures and comply with PN's constitution.
Meanwhile, Takiyuddin said PN was confident of winning the seats it contests in the upcoming Melaka election.
He said although seat allocation among the parties had yet to be finalised, PN would ensure that its candidates would not clash with those fielded by Barisan Nasional.
RoS yesterday confirmed it had cancelled PN's registration, saying the coalition's explanation failed to address the grounds for cancellation outlined in an earlier notice.
The decision was made under subparagraph 13(1)(c)(iv) of the Societies Act 1966 (Act 832), after the department reviewed documents and representations submitted by PN on Oct 12.
c3ebe63d60bffb5a: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysia Checkpoints and Border Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain arrived at the Sepang Magistrate’s Court this morning to face two charges of assault linked to an altercation with two Special Branch officers at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).

Security was tight across the court grounds, with an augmented contingent of police and Rela personnel restricting compound vehicle access strictly to authorised court staff and law enforcement officers, NST reported.

Dressed in a dark suit, the 54-year-old border agency chief appeared calm and composed upon his arrival. He made a stop at the court cafeteria for breakfast ahead of the proceedings, warmly extending an invitation to waiting press photographers and reporters to join him.
Lending a show of solidarity at the court complex was Port Klang MCBA commander Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal.

Shuhaily is set to face two counts of voluntarily causing hurt under Section 323 of the Penal Code for allegedly striking Lance Corporals Mohammad Faiz Muhamad Saman, 40, and Muhammad Ekmal Sofwan Driman.
If convicted, the offence is punishable by a prison term of up to one year, a maximum fine of RM2,000, or both. Criminal defence lawyer Kitson Foong is appearing for Shuhaily.

The charges stem from a high-profile confrontation at KLIA Terminal 1 on Sept 28, which thrust the agency into the spotlight after mobile footage went viral online. The clip appeared to capture a senior official matching Shuhaily’s likeness berating two men at the terminal, with one of the officers seemingly grabbed forcefully by the ears.
Following the viral uproar, Shuhaily publicly said on Oct 1 that he was prepared to bear full responsibility and accept whatever determination the government reached regarding the episode.

The case progressed to court following an intensive review between investigators and the prosecution. Police initially recorded statements from 25 witnesses before submitting the investigation papers to the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC).

Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar returned the dossier on Oct 8 for supplementary work, leading Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail to confirm on Oct 17 that prosecutors had demanded further clarification before framing charges.

The legal fallout widened on Oct 12 when Faiz lodged a follow-up police report through his lawyers, Kamal Hisham Ja’afar and Muhammad Nor Tamrin. The report claimed new evidence, alleging that his smartphone was confiscated while he attempted to photograph the airport dispute.

The two Special Branch personnel, deployed as travel control officers at the international gateway, have strenuously rejected suggestions that they were touting or facilitating “counter setting” syndicates to bypass immigration controls.
2a52467a4654f634: PARIS, Oct 21 — Vitinha’s superb late strike proved crucial as reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain saw off rivals Barcelona 4-2 yesterday in a dramatic game between two of the leading contenders to win this season’s Champions League.

The match was poised at 2-2 when the Portuguese playmaker, who came third in last year’s Ballon d’Or ranking, controlled on his chest and fired in from just outside the box in the 81st minute at the Parc des Princes.
Fabian Ruiz then sealed PSG’s third victory in as many outings in this season’s competition, as they aim to win the Champions League for the third season running.
It had briefly looked as though Barcelona would leave with a point when Lamine Yamal, who is hoping to win this year’s Ballon d’Or, stabbed in Barcelona’s second equaliser on the night.
Desire Doue had earlier opened the scoring for PSG, and Lucas Hernandez got their second goal after teenager Xavi Espart netted for the Catalans.
The defeat is a setback for Barcelona, albeit not one that is likely to seriously hurt their prospects of advancing further in Europe.
They had travelled to France on a run of 11 consecutive wins this season. That sequence is over, but the goals keep coming, and Yamal’s strike was Barcelona’s 50th of the campaign.
“I think it was a fantastic game from both teams but we made too many mistakes,” said Barcelona coach Hansi Flick.
“But I also saw a lot of good things. It was a great test for us and we have to learn from this game. Today, in October, you cannot win titles. You win the Champions League in June.”
PSG have now won seven games in a row altogether, but they lost both Ousmane Dembele — last year’s Ballon d’Or winner — and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to injury.
It remains to be seen how seriously hurt they are, although Doue was the real star here and Luis Enrique’s team are well set to comfortably reach the knockout phase anyway.
“It is just the start of the season and there will be a lot more big matches but the hunger is there and we will keep our focus,” Doue told broadcaster Canal Plus.

This was the 14th meeting of the teams in the Champions League in the last 13 years, and for Barcelona it was probably not their biggest game this week — beat Real Madrid on Sunday and they go nine points ahead of their great rivals in La Liga.
Rodri on bench, Dembele injured
That helps explain why Rodri, the 2024 Ballon d’Or winner, was on the bench at kick-off, although Raphinha was back in the line-up after a spell out.

Fresh from winning 4-2 at Manchester City last week, PSG almost scored inside 90 seconds as Kvaratskhelia hit the post, but they were dealt a blow as Dembele came off after just 20 minutes with a hamstring injury.
Ferran Torres replaced him, coming on against his former club, who themselves then lost Dani Olmo to injury.

Paris opened the scoring in the 38th minute following an error by Yamal — he gave away possession in his own half, and the ball came to Doue who showed superb footwork before firing into the bottom corner from just outside the area.
The home side were worthy of their lead at the interval, yet Barcelona drew level soon after half-time as Fermin Lopez released Espart who drove into the box and fired in his second senior goal.
Rodri soon entered the fray for Barca but the game became increasingly unbridled and Torres hit the post for the hosts just before Hernandez headed them back in front from a corner.
The defender was called into the side to mark Yamal in the absence of usual starting left-back Nuno Mendes. The goal was just his third for PSG, and a first since February 2024.
That crowned a fine performance for Hernandez, but he was substituted moments later by coach Luis Enrique, and replacement Warren Zaire-Emery was at fault for Barcelona’s second equaliser.
He got caught underneath a high ball, allowing Yamal to run away and stab in his 10th goal this season.
PSG had the last laugh, though, as they reminded their opponents that they remain the team to beat in Europe this season with Vitinha making it 3-2 before Ruiz secured the win. — AFP
dcb7ef98c27530b5: BEIJING: Oil prices edged higher on Wednesday on Middle East supply concerns, with traders wary of Red Sea shipping risks and threats to oil infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.
Brent crude futures rose 85 cents, or 0.78 per cent, to US$109.64 per barrel as of 0022 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 76 cents, or 0.78 per cent, to US$98.58 per barrel.

A supertanker caught fire after striking a sea mine south of the Strait of Hormuz while "violating" Iranian regulations, Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said on Tuesday, according to Iranian media. There were at least 18 vessel attacks reported over two weeks, shiptracker Kpler said in a note on Monday.

"Attacks on tankers have expanded beyond the Strait of Hormuz," LSEG analysts said in a note. "Iran has been targeting vessels as far south as the Gulf of Oman, threatening loadings outside of the Arab Gulf, as well as the ship-to-ship transfers that have helped to support Middle East loadings as the conflict has dragged on."
The Houthis on Monday claimed responsibility for attacks on a Saudi Aramco site in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield and Saudi Arabia's Riyadh and Abha airports.
The death toll from a Houthi attack on Yemeni government forces on Monday rose to 73 as fighting intensified.
Prices had fallen in the previous trading session after Iran's president discussed mediation efforts in a meeting with Pakistan's army chief in Tehran.

On Tuesday, Brent crude futures settled down 76 cents, or 0.69 per cent, at US$108.79, after touching a five-month high of US$111.99. The November contract for US West Texas Intermediate crude, which expired on Tuesday, settled down US$1.87, or 1.8 per cent, at US$101.79.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said in a television interview aired on Tuesday that Iran has not received a response from Saudi Arabia or Yemen's Houthis to its offer to help broker peace talks.
In the US, two Energy Department officials said on Tuesday they were working with refiners around the world to boost fuel output as a diesel shortage has raised prices.

US crude oil stockpiles were expected to have fallen last week along with product inventories, an extended Reuters poll showed on Tuesday. Eight analysts polled by Reuters estimated, on average, that crude inventories fell by about 800,000 barrels in the week ended Oct 16.
1091e5f190233729: MANCHESTER, Oct 21 — Enzo Maresca said Phil Foden provided evidence that his prolonged slump might finally be over with a hat-trick in Manchester City’s 5-1 rout of AEK Athens in the Champions League yesterday.
After struggling badly over the last two seasons, England playmaker Foden could be on the brink of a long-awaited renaissance after his sublime display at the Etihad Stadium.
It has been a trying period for the 26-year-old, who has admitted suffering with mental health issues.
Foden fell out of favour with former City boss Pep Guardiola and hadn’t scored for 10 months prior to his goal in Saturday’s Premier League win against Ipswich.
This season has been another turbulent experience for Foden, who was sent off in City’s win at Manchester United and had been forced to battle for a place in Maresca’s staring line-up.

Taking advantage of injuries that left Erling Haaland on the bench against AEK and sidelined Antoine Semenyo for eight weeks, Foden starred on the left wing before switching to the ‘false nine’ role as the focal point of City’s attack.
“It is good news for me because you know he is doing well and this is what we want for many reasons,” City boss Maresca said.
“First of all, because he is a top player and we know that. Happy for him, but also happy for the team that we have one more weapon that we can use.”
Foden’s hat-trick will surely have caught England manager Thomas Tuchel’s eye as he prepares to pick his squad for the Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain in November.
Long heralded as one of England’s brightest talents, Foden was left out of his country’s World Cup squad earlier this year in a damning sign of his fall from grace.
Having ended his run without a goal in the Champions League since November 2025, Foden now has to produce nights like this on a regular basis to earn the trust of Maresca and Tuchel.
‘Slowly but surely’
Rico Lewis delivered the assists for Foden’s first two goals and the right-back hailed his friend and former youth academy colleague’s prodigious talent.
“Phil is an unbelievable player. When I first came into the first team, I was closest with him,” Lewis said.
“I almost wanted to be him when I was coming up. To be able to play with him now, five years down the line and assist him and see how well he’s still doing, is amazing.”
Foden’s dazzling contribution against the out-classed Greeks wasn’t limited to his treble.
He also teed up Rayan Cherki for City’s third goal with a typically smooth pass.
Finally playing with a smile on his face again, Foden said: “I enjoyed that a lot. The lads were great.
“Probably the second goal was my favourite, the way it went in. Delighted to score goals. I am a forward, so I have to keep scoring and helping the team. It’s good for my confidence.”
Foden acknowledged his substantial loss of form as he discussed his belief that a brighter future is within his grasp.
“Slowly, but surely. Still got a long way to go, but I am going in the right direction,” he said.
“Scoring along the way definitely helps. I want to keep working hard and keep being the best I can for the manager and the team.
“When I changed into that false nine role I enjoyed it a lot. Really enjoyed that role tonight.”
Foden is rarely been a vocal leader but he believes playing with several of City’s youngsters in Maresca’s much-changed team against AEK forced him to play with more maturity.
“Trying to help them the best I can with the captains. Try (to) help the young ones, and it shows the trust the manager has,” he said.
It might only have been baby steps against AEK, but Foden is finally on the road to redemption. — AFP
1a7faba15b214145: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 —The government is open to considering a proposal to establish a Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into the Retirement Fund (Incorporated) (KWAP) and the Employees Provident Fund (EPF), should the need arise.

Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said this would apply if there is concrete information, evidence, or findings indicating a necessity for a comprehensive and independent public inquiry.

She added that the government remains committed to ensuring that any issues concerning the management of public funds including aspects of governance and investment decisions are examined based on facts and evidence, through appropriate oversight mechanisms.
“If the findings indicate a clear public need and interest for a special inquiry, a proposal to establish a Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) may be duly considered.

“In determining the necessity for an RCI whether it concerns institutions that manage public funds or any other institution the government takes into account public interest, the gravity of the issue, as well as available facts and evidence,” she said in a written reply to the Dewan Rakyat, which was published on the Parliament’s website today.

Azalina made these remarks in response to a question from Datuk Seri Dr. Shahidan Kassim (PN-Arau) regarding whether the government is prepared to consider establishing an RCI concerning KWAP (Retirement Fund Incorporated) and the EPF (Employees Provident Fund) in relation to their governance, investment management, or questionable financial decisions.

Addressing Shahidan’s query on the criteria used to determine the need for an RCI into institutions that manage public funds, Azalina explained that the prevailing Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) require such a proposal to be submitted via a Cabinet Memorandum by the lead ministry.
“The memorandum is then submitted for Cabinet approval. Once approved, the Prime Minister will present the proposal to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong to seek His Majesty’s consent.

“If consent is granted, the establishment of the RCI will involve defining its terms of reference, membership, and the duration of the inquiry. These details are subsequently finalised through a gazette notification in the Federal Government Gazette before the RCI commences its functions,” she said. — Bernama
7b31f7d23e44df60: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Every culture (and perhaps nation) has its own dumplings, whether it’s Shanghai’s calling card of xiao long bao, tortellinis made by Italian nonnas, Japanese gyoza and the list goes on.
Each fold tells a story of flavour, tradition and love in every bite.

Dumpling Daddies by Jonathan Ooi and Victor Yap is what happens when you start with a familiar flavour, pull apart everything — the wrapper, filling and even accompaniments like sauce and pickles — then build it all back again to create a truly unique dumpling.
Their eye-catching Ipoh Mali Chicken Gnocchi is a prime example.
It features mini chickens shaped from chewy taro swimming in a delicious bowl of chicken stock laced with prawn oil, shredded chicken, and, of course, stubby crunchy bean sprouts.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Ipoh Mali Chicken Gnocchi (left) reimagines 'kai si hor fun' with mini chicken-shaped taro dumplings. Teba-Gyoza (right) isn't your ordinary grilled chicken wing as it's stuffed with Thai 'haw mok'. — Pictures by Ryonn Leong
Yes, the chicken dumplings take the place of noodles in this iconic dish paying homage to Ipoh’s kai si hor fun.
Everything with Malaysian flavours is fair game for the duo but they have one thing they hold sacred: it must be a proper meal, not gimmicky.
“Anything that can be wrapped — not necessarily with flour — it could be translucent or even a rice dumpling wrapped in a leaf, we just want it to be fun.”
The seed for Dumpling Daddies was planted in a Tokyo cafe one evening last year. Yap was on holiday there with friends and Ooi was at that time working in the mega city.
They coincidentally discovered a shared dream of opening a dumpling shop envisioned as a neighbourhood place people would keep returning to.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Laksa Lemak Prawn Ravioli (left) uses a 'jiaozi' wrapper to encase prawns in a rich laksa broth. Sweet & Sticky Beef 'Epok-Epok' (right) is a crispy vessel for a filling of Daging Masak Hitam Sarawak that uses raisins. — Pictures by Ryonn Leong

This dream took off when Ooi returned to Kuala Lumpur this year, as he is on a micro retirement from a two-decade-long career in beauty, luxury and creative brand development that started in Kuala Lumpur and expanded to Singapore, Hong Kong, Shanghai and Tokyo.

Of the two, Yap, a trained civil and structural engineer, is the one with an extensive F&B background having co-founded the now-closed Tray Cafe, Fittie Sense, Peaches & Cream and apricot by Peaches and Cream.
Together they wanted to explore food through an Asian lens with Dumpling Daddies.
They are like two sides of a coin: Ooi’s creative mind comes out with the unique dumplings and the branding while Yap keeps him grounded with the techniques and real life F&B experience.
And in case you are wondering, neither are real-life daddies but they occupy an awkward age bracket: too young to be “uncles” and too old to be “bros”; hence, “daddies” was chosen.
“The interesting thing about it is when dad takes over a kitchen, it’s chaotic and experimental like a fun concept,” Ooi explained.
They debuted their dumplings at a collaborative food party themed “Campur-Campur” at Dou Dou Bake in Petaling Jaya in September.
It was a collaboration with two friends: Chef Piyanat “Gugs” Yowabut of Homm House No. 8 and Melanie Kang of Mel’s Memory Kitchen.
Gugs hosts his Thai supper club in PJ Section 17 while Kang does private lunches featuring Hakka and Peranakan dishes beloved by her own family.
The Malaysian-style pop-up puts the best offerings on a table, allowing diners to feast on all kinds of food from different cultures and flavours that celebrate our diversity.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Crispy Puri Bombs with Snapper Umai (left) offered the perfect one-bite combination of crunch and freshness. Cheers to Dumpling Daddies (right) for a fun party of dumplings, salads and grilled items.— Pictures by Dou Dou Bake and Ryonn Leong

As Dumpling Daddies worked on the dumplings, Gugs and Kang came up with platters of grilled meat, seafood and side dishes like Nyonya acar and Gai Yang skewers while Dou Dou Bake provided the desserts and drinks.

Diners sampled the Laksa Lemak Prawn Ravioli, which originally started as a Teochew fish skin dumpling but changed into a prawn jiaozi in ravioli form, sitting in a creamy laksa sauce with fresh herbs and relish
Sweet & Sticky Beef Epok-Epok took many trials to get the crispy pastry right, until it was strong enough to hold the sweet sticky Daging Masak Hitam Sarawak.
A permanent home for Dumpling Daddies is still in the works but in the meantime, the duo plans to cook and collaborate more with others to learn what diners want.
“Ultimately we want to have fun with it,” Yap said.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Look out for the Encore edition of 'Campur-Campur' to be held from November 7 to 9, featuring (from left to right) Chef Gugs of Homm House No. 8, Victor Yap, Melanie Kang of Mel's Memory Kitchen and Jonathan Ooi. — Picture courtesy of Dumpling Daddies.

For those who missed out on the last party, an encore of “Campur-Campur” will take place from November 7 to 9, at In the Muments (IG:@inthemument), an event space next to Air Day Coffee (IG:@airday_coffee).
Tweaks have been made to the menu, following feedback and observations from the first “Campur-Campur”.
Their Edition 01 menu will be a six-course sharing experience featuring 11 dishes, with adjusted portions and a format allowing everyone to try the full menu.

Reservations will go online at Air Day Coffee and Dumpling Daddies Instagram starting October 24 so secure your spot quickly. The first three-night party at Dou Dou was fully booked in 24 hours, so don’t say we didn’t warn you.

896095b854839e17: OCTOBER 21 — I walked past a motorcycle workshop the other day and saw it had chained the grates over the nearby drains.
Makes sense, I thought, and kept walking.
Years ago, someone had stolen the grate cover in front of my gate, which had my brother fall right into the drain in the dark.
Nothing was safe if it was made from metal in those days but now instead of plundering scrap metal, thieves are risking electrocution for a risky payload with a huge payoff.
I hear talk they’re trying to stop cable theft by increasing penalties but let me ask you this — when have penalties ever stopped people when the reward is bigger than the risk?
It makes me sad sometimes (or maybe I’ve just been successfully indoctrinated by all the anti-dadah propaganda of the 80s) that even with the huge penalties for drug trafficking, it still happens.
When you consider your life being worth less than money, it’s just tragic.
Snatch theft became less of a common incident in the Klang Valley when delivery services gained momentum.
Why steal a purse for uncertain returns when you could go around with your bike for fixed payments?
Now the delivery companies are beginning to reduce payouts, making delivery jobs a lot less enticing.
With so many delivery platforms and the existence of emails, becoming a dispatch rider for a company is no longer an option for young school leavers.
Why pay someone a set amount when you can probably contract a company to do the same, often for cheaper?
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
A Cable Theft Security Patrol is seen at the MRT Taman Naga Emas station in Bandar Tasik Selatan, Kuala Lumpur on April 11, 2026. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
Now people are willing to risk their lives to steal cables, likely backed by shady figures looking to rake in millions by recruiting the poor and desperate.
Yes, rail companies need to be smarter about securing their cables. Technology exists. Sensors, cameras, monitoring systems — all that can be implemented.
Yet what rail companies cannot control is the socioeconomic factors that encourage the thefts.
I look at the videos of young people rampaging on the streets of Paris and see the derisive comments.
Yes, I do think it’s unfair that small business owners had their storefronts destroyed alongside large companies whose insurance will cover all the damage.
The solution is not increasing the policing or further oppressing the disenfranchised.
It is well-documented how lopsided the distribution of income has become and income disparity has only increased in recent years.
Now AI has not empowered anyone but the rich tech oligarchs making money from ridiculous overvaluations while many are losing their jobs.
Sometimes I sigh seeing the businessmen who are convinced that people like me can be replaced with a bot.
While it is important to snuff out these rogue agents targeting power and communication cables, disincentivizing theft by making easy money less attractive is the better strategy in the long run.
If you want people to make better choices, then make them available. Make crime, heists so unpalatable in comparison to a comfortable living situation.
Few people are more dangerous than the ones with nothing left to lose and that is something leaders everywhere should note, especially after the Paris riots.­
* This is the personal opinion of the columnist.
bcba74bd029582ab: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 6,346 MyKiosk units nationwide, or 88 per cent of the 7,243 units provided under the programme, were occupied and operational as of August.

Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said the remaining 897 units, or 12 per cent, were vacant, based on data and operational reports submitted by state governments and local authorities.

"The MyKiosk programme, implemented through the Local Government Department, aims to improve the socioeconomic status of local traders by providing standardised, safe and conducive business premises at affordable rental rates," he said in a written parliamentary reply published on Parliament's website yesterday.
A total of RM150 million was allocated under the 2023 and 2024 Budgets for MyKiosk 1.0 and 2.0, covering 7,243 units nationwide.

Nga said the ministry was working closely with local authorities to increase occupancy rates and ensure the kiosks were fully utilised, with four strategic measures being implemented to address vacancies.
These included establishing an internal task force to conduct regular, coordinated inspections to assess the suitability of kiosk locations and expedite the process of filling vacant units.
He said the ministry was also holding targeted discussions with local authorities to resolve local issues and allowing them to apply for additional allocations for kiosk maintenance and repairs.
"In addition, a strict traffic-light system has been introduced, with MyKiosk occupancy performance used as a benchmark for approving future projects.
"Local authorities recording poor occupancy performance, classified under the Red Zone, will not be considered for approval of new projects."

Nga said ensuring every MyKiosk unit was fully utilised remained a priority, adding that the ministry would continue to implement interventions, monitoring and follow-up measures with local authorities to improve occupancy rates.
0ef134451db1b9fd: MELBOURNE: Australia's federal police chief warned on Wednesday of growing extremism online fuelling political polarisation after an attack on lawmaker Helen Haines, who remains in a critical condition in a Melbourne hospital.
Australian Federal Police (AFP) Commissioner Krissy Barrett said there is "a growing sort of level of extremist views, and particularly in the online space".

"The current criminal threat environment is febrile, and when it comes to federal parliamentarians, the AFP continues to record the growing volume of online abuse, threatening rhetoric, and intimidation," she added.
Haines is fighting for her life in a hospital in Melbourne after being struck on Monday near her office in the town of Wangaratta, just over 200km (124 miles) northeast of the Victoria state capital.
Prime minister Anthony Albanese has led an outpouring of support for Haines, who was widely praised for her efforts to increase transparency in politics and crack down on corruption.

Her attack has also sparked soul-searching in a country where political violence is rare but police have documented a steady rise in threats and abuse directed towards elected officials in recent years.
The independent lawmaker, 65, was standing near the trunk of her car when she was struck by a Toyota Land Cruiser on Monday afternoon.
The 43-year-old male driver of the vehicle was known to police.

He was charged on Tuesday with dangerous driving causing serious injury and intentionally causing serious injury, as well as the federal crime of harming a public official, which carries a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison.
"Police will allege the incident was targeted," Victoria police said.
The man will appear in court in Wangaratta on Wednesday.
8ac73309772ab3fb: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is open to considering a Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into the Retirement Fund Incorporated (KWAP) and the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) if credible information or evidence warrants a comprehensive and independent investigation.

Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said issues involving the management of public funds, including governance and investment decisions, would continue to be examined based on facts and evidence through appropriate oversight mechanisms.

"Should further scrutiny establish a clear need and public interest in a special investigation, the proposal to establish an RCI may be considered accordingly," she said in a written parliamentary reply.

Azalina was responding to Datuk Seri Dr Shahidan Kassim (Pas-Arau), who asked whether the government was prepared to consider an RCI into KWAP and EPF over governance, investment management or questionable financial decisions.
Shahidan also sought clarification on the criteria used by the government to determine whether an RCI was necessary for institutions managing public funds.
Azalina said the establishment of an RCI was subject to the Commissions of Inquiry Act 1950 and procedures prescribed by the government.
"Under the standard operating procedures, a proposal to establish an RCI must be submitted through a Cabinet Memorandum by the lead ministry for consideration and approval by the Cabinet.
"Once approved, the prime minister will submit the proposal to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong for royal consent.

"Upon obtaining consent, the RCI's terms of reference, membership and duration of the inquiry will be determined and finalised through publication in the Federal Government Gazette before it begins its work," she said.

She said the government would consider the public interest, seriousness of the issues, available facts and evidence, and the need for an independent and comprehensive investigation when deciding whether to establish an RCI, whether into institutions managing public funds or any other institution.
edd471aad66da224: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Wednesday, supported by strong domestic economic data that strengthened expectations of a possible normalisation of the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR).

17fc37bda259bde1: KUALA LUMPUR: After a non-stop year on set, actress Sophia Albarakbah is stepping back from the spotlight for a month-long break to spend quality time with her family and lay the groundwork for her upcoming business venture.
Sophia, 33, said the breather is a much-needed pause to recharge before diving back into her acting commitments.

She explained that her gruelling filming schedule had left her with little personal time, making this sabbatical the ideal opportunity to reconnect with loved ones and map out her entrepreneurial plans.

"When you are caught up with continuous filming, free time with family becomes a rare luxury. So, I want to take this opportunity to rest, spend time with them and strategise for my business," she said.
"I have to manage my time wisely to ensure that my acting career and my passion for business can move forward hand in hand.

"God willing, the business will be launched next year. Taking a break is also essential to avoid burnout after back-to-back shoots," she added at the recent launch of the Anugerah Melodi Terhangat (AMT) 2026 X Cuckootopia event at Hyatt Regency Kuala Lumpur.
Reflecting on her journey, Sophia was happy that public attention has shifted from her personal life to her professional acting roles.

Unfazed by rumours that her star power is dimming due to a lack of headlines, Sophia insists her priority is building a lasting legacy through solid work rather than chasing fleeting fame through gossip.
"Let people say my name is fading or whatever simply because there are no sensational stories about me, as long as I remain active in my craft and intentionally steer clear of unnecessary drama.
"I don't like it when people know me for unpleasant or untrue matters, so I am far more comfortable living like this," she said.
866d71ef1272a509: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is strengthening its role in global seabed mapping by hosting an international meeting and data sprint. The event brings together experts from 33 countries to advance ocean mapping and data sharing.
Royal Malaysian Navy chief Admiral Tan Sri Dr Zulhelmy Ithnain officiated at the opening of the Seabed 2030 Indo-Pacific Ocean Mapping Meeting and Data Sprint 2026 here.
The event saw the signing of a memorandum of understanding on the Melaka and Singapore Straits Electronic Navigational Charts and a Seabed 2030 data-sharing agreement.

The signatories included National Hydrographic Centre director-general Rear Admiral Dr Najhan Md Said, Indonesian Navy Hydro-Oceanographic Centre (Pushidrosal) Commodore Edward Halomoan Sibuea and Japan Hydrographic Association representative Dr Masayuki Fujita. A representative of Singapore's Maritime and Port Authority and Nippon Foundation-GEBCO Seabed 2030 Project director Jamie McMichael-Phillips also signed the agreements.
Organised by the NHC, the event has attracted 250 participants from 33 countries, including hydrographers, government representatives, research institutions and maritime industry players.
The plenary session runs until today, followed by a data sprint today and tomorrow. The sprint provides hands-on experience in preparing, demonstrating and integrating bathymetric data.
Zulhelmy said the ocean was central to Malaysia's identity, economy and security.
"For Malaysia, the ocean is fundamental to who we are. Our geography, economy, security and future are inseparable from the maritime domain.
"Effective maritime policy begins with knowledge. We cannot manage what we do not understand. We cannot protect what we cannot see."

The Nippon Foundation-GEBCO Seabed 2030 Project aims to accelerate the mapping of the world's seabed by 2030. Up to April, only 28.7 per cent of the ocean floor had been mapped to modern standards, leaving more than 70 per cent inadequately mapped.
"This is a significant knowledge gap with implications for science, development and security," said Zulhelmy.

He thanked Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim for the allocation in the 2027 Budget to acquire two new survey motor launches, saying the vessels would expedite hydrographic survey operations and help address priority data gaps.
Zulhelmy also thanked the National Security Council for facilitating approval for Malaysia's first national research vessel, describing it as a strategic investment in the country's maritime future.
On data sharing, he said arrangements must respect national requirements, security considerations, data ownership and agreed conditions of use.
"This gathering can boost Malaysia's role as a regional hub for seabed mapping and marine geospatial cooperation," he said.
In a separate address, Najhan said the meeting built on a Seabed 2030 gathering held in Nadi, Fiji, in 2024.
"I sincerely hope that every delegate will return home with valuable insights, new skills and practical experiences."
807cd6cdd4d4152d: From P Sundramoorthy

The high-profile investigation into the MBI International Group investment scheme raises a fundamental question about Malaysia’s response to major financial crime: what happens after arrests, raids, and the seizure or freezing of billions of ringgit in assets?
Under Op Northern Star, police announced the arrests of individuals suspected of facilitating the movement or laundering of funds linked to the alleged investment fraud.
By May 2025, authorities reported that 17 people were detained and assets worth approximately RM3.81 billion had been seized or frozen.
Subsequent reporting in January 2026 indicated that 23 people were arrested, with authorities pursuing the forfeiture of hundreds of properties and funds held in bank accounts.

These are significant developments. However, the public deserves clarity about whether investigations are progressing towards lawful outcomes and whether affected investors can realistically expect to recover their losses.
The MBI case should not be judged solely by the number of arrests or the value of assets seized. The real test is what follows.

Complex financial crime investigations require investigators to trace funds, establish individual responsibilities, examine corporate transactions and determine whether assets represent proceeds of unlawful activities.
The reported international dimension of the MBI case adds further challenges, including obtaining foreign evidence and coordinating with overseas enforcement agencies.

An arrest does not establish guilt, and a frozen asset does not automatically represent criminal proceeds. Similarly, release from remand does not necessarily mean a suspect has been cleared or that an investigation has ended.
However, these distinctions should not become a reason for prolonged public uncertainty.
Transparency without compromising investigations

When those previously detained in high-profile investigations return to their daily activities or retain prominent business and social positions, questions inevitably arise. Some may assume allegations have been dismissed, while others may suspect preferential treatment for influential individuals.

Neither conclusion should be drawn merely from a person's release or continued public presence. The presumption of innocence must be respected, and allegations must be established through proper legal proceedings.
The police should provide periodic updates while the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission should clarify the status of any related investigation within its jurisdiction.
Where legally permissible, updates should explain whether investigation papers have been referred to prosecutors and whether charges or asset forfeiture proceedings have commenced.

Where investigations have concluded or decisions have been made not to pursue particular individuals, appropriate clarification should be provided, subject to legal restrictions and the rights of those concerned.
Victims must not be forgotten

Perhaps the most important consideration is the position of investors who lost money through the MBI scheme. Announcements of billions of ringgit in seized or frozen assets may create expectations that investors will eventually recover their losses.
However, the value of seized assets does not necessarily represent the amount available for distribution to victims.
Assets may be subject to competing claims, ownership disputes and forfeiture proceedings. Their eventual recovery and distribution depend on applicable law and the outcomes of legal proceedings.
Authorities should communicate realistic expectations about asset recovery and explain, within legal limits, what mechanisms are available to address victims' claims.
Op Metal a broader lesson

The importance of following investigations through to their outcomes is also illustrated by Op Metal, a separate MACC operation launched in July 2025 targeting an alleged scrap metal and electronic waste smuggling syndicate.

Authorities seized assets worth over RM183 million and froze company and individual bank accounts containing approximately RM51 million. The suspected activities were estimated to have caused the government more than RM950 million in lost export tax revenue over six years.
Op Metal is unrelated to the MBI investment scheme investigation. However, it reinforces a broader lesson: seizures and enforcement announcements are only part of the process.

The MBI case warrants particular attention because of the financial losses suffered by investors and the importance of maintaining confidence in Malaysia's handling of major investment-related fraud allegations.
It presents an opportunity for Malaysian authorities to demonstrate that complex, cross-border financial crime can be confronted with determination, professionalism and transparency.
Ultimately, the public does not expect investigators to reveal everything, but it does expect them to explain what can responsibly be disclosed, demonstrate progress and communicate lawful outcomes.
Justice must extend beyond the headlines.
P Sundramoorthy is a criminologist at the Centre for Policy Research at Universiti Sains Malaysia and an FMT reader.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
83b07be6d86794cd: IPOH: For many older Malaysians, staying in their own home is an important part of retaining independence. But as more senior citizens begin living alone, a more uncomfortable question is emerging - who notices when something goes wrong?
According to the National Health and Morbidity Survey 2025, 18.8% of Malaysians aged 60 and above - about 770,800 people - now live alone, up from 6.3% in 2018.

At the same time, only about 600,000 of the country’s 4.2 million senior citizens meet the health ministry’s criteria for “healthy ageing”, which include being able to live independently, having strong social support and keeping chronic illnesses under control.
The concern is not simply loneliness: falls, sudden illness or loss of consciousness can become far more dangerous when there is nobody nearby to notice or summon help.
Gerontological counselling expert Dr Hapsah Yusof said Malaysia could learn from Japan, where technology is used alongside community-based care to support older people living alone.

“Japan’s experience in addressing kodokushi, or ‘lonely death’, shows that technology needs to go hand in hand with community care systems, regular visits and the registration of senior citizens at the local authority level,” she told Bernama.

Smartwatches that monitor heart rate and other health indicators are already widely available, but Hapsah believes devices designed specifically for older users could go further. Features such as fall detection, alerts for unusual movement and emergency notifications could be linked directly to family members, caregivers or response teams.

Such technology could be particularly useful for older people at risk of falls. Local studies have recorded fall rates of between 4.07% and 14.1% among elderly Malaysians, with those living alone facing more than twice the risk of those living with family.
A separate study at a local medical centre found that nearly one in four older patients who had suffered a fall died within a year from related complications.
Knowing who may need help

Technology alone, however, cannot solve the problem if nobody knows who is vulnerable in the first place. Hapsah proposed an integrated database bringing together information from agencies such as the social welfare department, police, fire and rescue department, local authorities and community leaders.

At present, records involving older people found dead alone are kept separately by different agencies. A shared system, she said, could help identify high-risk individuals earlier and trigger follow-up before a crisis occurs.
For example, a system could flag an older person who lives alone, has health problems or has recently required assistance, then prompt the relevant agency or community network to check in.

The idea sounds straightforward, but Hapsah acknowledged that access would be uneven. Cost, limited internet connectivity, low digital literacy, privacy concerns and language barriers could all prevent the people most at risk from benefiting.
That means any rollout would need to be accompanied by age-friendly interfaces, digital training and support for older users who are less comfortable with technology.
The discussion goes beyond wearable devices. PLANMalaysia director-general Dr Alias Rameli said ageing should become a more central part of how Malaysia thinks about smart cities.
Instead of creating a separate system for older people, he believes age-friendly planning should be built into housing, transport, health services and infrastructure from the start.

The Draft Physical Planning Guidelines for the Elderly 2026 already refer to technologies such as emergency buttons, fall detectors, motion sensors, telehealth, medication reminders and communication platforms connecting senior citizens with family members or caregivers.
Alias said Perak could be a natural place to test such ideas because it has the highest proportion of residents aged 65 and above in Malaysia.

A “smart ageing” township, in his view, would combine technology with housing that supports ageing in place, local emergency response, accessible services and better coordination between health, welfare and community networks.

“A truly smart city should not only be capable of detecting emergencies but also create an environment that enables people to age safely and be active and independent while remaining an integral part of the community,” he said.
That final point may be the most important: a sensor can detect a fall, and an emergency button can summon help, but neither can replace regular human contact.
The strongest safety net for someone ageing alone is likely to be a combination of both - technology that can raise the alarm when needed, and people who are already paying attention.
057bb0c77e5d879a: KUALA LUMPUR: Kesesakan berjam-jam terutama pada hujung minggu dan musim perayaan, bukan perkara asing bagi pengguna Lebuhraya Kuala Lumpur-Karak (KLK), antara laluan utama menghubungkan Lembah Klang dengan Pantai Timur.
Peningkatan jumlah kenderaan, pergerakan kenderaan berat yang lebih perlahan serta kemalangan atau kerosakan kenderaan sering menyebabkan aliran trafik di laluan berkenaan terganggu.

Bagi menangani masalah itu, Kementerian Kerja Raya (KKR) menerusi Lembaga Lebuhraya Malaysia (LLM) menyelia projek pelebaran KLK dan pembinaan Terowong Ketiga Genting Sempah oleh syarikat konsesi AFA Prime Bhd.
Projek bernilai RM2.1 bilion sepanjang 45.3km itu disasarkan siap sepenuhnya pada 2029.

Ia melibatkan pelebaran daripada tiga kepada empat lorong dari Plaza Tol Gombak hingga Genting Sempah, manakala laluan dari Genting Sempah ke Persimpangan Mempaga, Bentong, akan ditambah daripada dua kepada tiga lorong.
Projek itu turut merangkumi pembinaan Terowong Ketiga Genting Sempah sepanjang 999m.
Menteri Kerja Raya Alexander Nanta Linggi sebelum ini berkata kerja fizikal projek bermula pada 9 Mac lalu, selaras dengan tarikh mula pembinaan yang diluluskan LLM.
Pakar pengangkutan Wan Agyl Wan Hassan berkata usaha itu diperlukan kerana KLK kini menanggung jumlah trafik jauh lebih tinggi berbanding ketika laluan tersebut dinaik taraf pada 1997.
Pengasas dan penasihat kanan MY Mobility Vision itu berkata jumlah trafik meningkat daripada kira-kira 41,000 kenderaan sehari ketika itu kepada lebih 130,000 kenderaan sehari sekarang.

“Dengan tambahan satu lorong setiap hala, sudah tentu akan ada lebih banyak ruang untuk menampung trafik dan kita sepatutnya melihat aliran lebih baik, terutama pada hari biasa dan hujung minggu,” katanya kepada FMT.
Bagaimanapun, Wan Agyl berkata penambahan lorong sahaja tidak semestinya dapat menyelesaikan masalah kesesakan sepenuhnya.
Menurutnya, pembinaan terowong ketiga juga penting kerana Genting Sempah antara titik kesesakan utama di koridor KLK yang boleh memperlahankan keseluruhan perjalanan.
Antara lokasi kritikal ialah laluan KM32 hingga KM37, yang pernah mencatatkan kesesakan serius ketika waktu puncak hujung minggu.

Katanya, keadaan muka bumi berbukit menyebabkan lori dan kenderaan berat bergerak lebih perlahan, manakala perubahan lorong serta perbezaan kelajuan antara kenderaan turut menjejaskan kelancaran trafik.
Justeru, terowong baharu yang dibina menggunakan kaedah New Austrian Tunnelling Method (NATM) menjadi antara komponen penting projek bagi mengurangkan kesesakan di kawasan berkenaan.
“Apabila penambahan lorong dan terowong baharu dibuat bersama, kita sepatutnya mendapat aliran trafik yang lebih konsisten dan lancar,” katanya.
Tingkat keselamatan pengguna
Selain menambah kapasiti jalan, Wan Agyl berkata aspek keselamatan dan pengurusan insiden juga penting bagi memastikan trafik di KLK dapat bergerak lancar.
Menurutnya, kemalangan atau kerosakan kenderaan boleh menyebabkan kesesakan menjadi lebih buruk dalam tempoh singkat apabila satu daripada lorong sedia ada terhalang.

“Lebuh raya yang baik bukan sekadar berapa banyak lorong yang kita ada. Kita juga kena lihat seberapa cepat sistem boleh bertindak apabila berlaku sesuatu insiden dan seberapa cepat aliran trafik boleh dikembalikan kepada keadaan normal,” katanya.
Sehubungan itu, projek pelebaran berkenaan turut memberi perhatian kepada aspek keselamatan termasuk penyediaan bahu jalan, pencahayaan, peningkatan jarak penglihatan dan sistem pemantauan trafik.

Pada 3 Ogos lalu, Nanta berkata pemasangan lampu jalan di lokasi dikenal pasti sedang dilaksanakan secara berperingkat, bermula dari selepas Terowong Genting Sempah hingga Persimpangan Mempaga sejauh kira-kira 26km.
Sebanyak 297 lampu jalan LED berkuasa solar akan dipasang di lokasi berisiko menerusi inisiatif dibiayai LLM bagi meningkatkan keselamatan pengguna, khususnya pada waktu malam.
Inisiatif itu turut merangkumi penggunaan Smart Lighting System, kamera litar tertutup (CCTV) dan Vehicle Incident Detection System (VIDS).
Perjalanan lancar bantu perniagaan
Manfaat projek itu bukan hanya kepada pengguna jalan raya, malah dijangka turut dirasai sektor perniagaan yang bergantung pada KLK untuk pergerakan barangan antara Lembah Klang dan Pantai Timur.

Setiausaha Agung Persekutuan Persatuan Perniagaan Malaysia (FMBA) Munaver Ahmad Nazir Ahmad berkata kesesakan di KLK memberi kesan kepada operasi perniagaan, khususnya penghantaran barangan dan pergerakan pekerja.
“Kesan utama kepada perniagaan bukan hanya masa perjalanan yang lebih panjang, tetapi ketidakpastian masa ketibaan,” katanya.

Menurutnya, pelebaran lebuh raya itu berpotensi menjadikan masa perjalanan lebih konsisten, sekali gus membantu syarikat logistik, pengilang, pemborong, peruncit dan perusahaan kecil dan sederhana (PKS) merancang penghantaran dengan lebih tepat.
Beliau berkata hubungan jalan raya yang lebih baik juga boleh memperluas akses pasaran kepada usahawan di Pahang, Terengganu dan Kelantan, khususnya untuk memasarkan produk ke Lembah Klang.
Katanya, perjalanan yang lebih konsisten dapat memudahkan penghantaran produk tempatan seperti makanan, hasil pertanian, batik, kraf dan hasil perikanan.
Pengguna harap perjalanan lebih lancar
Pengguna KLK yang ditemui FMT turut berharap projek itu dapat mengurangkan kesesakan serta menjadikan perjalanan lebih lancar dan selamat.
Mohd Farid Ismail, 38, yang tinggal di Gombak dan menggunakan KLK setiap hari untuk berniaga, berharap penambahan lorong dapat mengurangkan kesesakan terutama pada hujung minggu dan cuti umum.
“Kita harap lepas ini kuranglah kesesakan bila jalan sudah lebih besar,” katanya.
Mekanik Syah Effendi Abdul Jalil, 43, pula berkata penambahan lorong boleh membantu mengurangkan gangguan trafik apabila berlaku kerosakan kenderaan berat.
“Di sini banyak lori. Kadang-kadang lori rosak dan menyebabkan kesesakan. Kalau tambah laluan, mungkin memang dapat membantu,” katanya.

Bagi Sharifah Nur Syuhada, 30, yang pernah mengambil masa sehingga tiga jam untuk bergerak dari kawasan Hentian Rehat dan Rawat (R&R) Genting Sempah ke Gombak, projek itu diharap dapat membawa perubahan ketara kepada pengguna.
“Harapnya projek pembesaran jalan ini dapat membantu melancarkan trafik dan mengurangkan kemalangan,” katanya.
25fe17c69c208bd0: KUALA LUMPUR: The haj waiting period could be more than halved, from about 150 years to less than 70, under the Haj Preparation Plan – Seruan Istito'ah.

Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the projected reduction was based on current estimates by Lembaga Tabung Haji, but could change depending on several factors.

"This depends on several factors, including the number of depositors who meet the prescribed minimum savings requirement, Malaysia's official haj quota in the future and developments in the Holy Land.
"Depositors who had already registered for haj would be given a transition period of more than two years, until Dec 31, 2028, to meet the minimum savings requirement of RM15,000.

"From Jan 1, 2029, the haj waiting list will be systematically and automatically reorganised according to registration dates among depositors who have achieved the minimum savings threshold," he said in a written parliamentary reply.

Zulkifli was responding to Abdul Latiff Abdul Rahman (Pas-Kuala Krai), who asked about the actual waiting period for depositors who had reached the RM15,000 minimum savings threshold, as well as the status of those who had registered long ago but had yet to accumulate the required amount.
Zulkifli said depositors who had registered but had yet to meet the RM15,000 requirement would be included in the active haj waiting list once they fulfilled the savings requirement.
a33e402596121e7d: LONDON: Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has accused Cristiano Ronaldo of letting the team down during his time in charge.
Portugal star Ronaldo was in his second spell at United when Ten Hag was hired in 2022.
Ten Hag's relationship with Ronaldo quickly became tense and the striker refused to come on as a substitute in a win over Tottenham in the October 2022.
Ronaldo was dropped for a subsequent match against Chelsea, prompting him to give an explosive television interview in which he said he felt betrayed by United and did not respect Ten Hag.
The former Real Madrid forward's contract at United was mutually terminated the following month.
"He let the team down, and he let me down, because we planned with him," Ten Hag said in an interview with The Athletic.
"Obviously, he's one of the best in football history. I respected him a lot. But at that time, as a manager, I had to make a rational decision and keep the players I admire in."
Ten Hag said Ronaldo pulled out of training sessions and did not complete the full run that players were set after they were beaten 4-0 by Brentford early in his reign.

"I confronted him with this. Many times I say, 'Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can't bring yourself in the box, you can't score'. He was not capable to do this," Ten Hag said.
"It's the wrong idea to put this to me that I expected him to do the pressing, that he's exhausted. But he couldn't.
"He ran neither in possession nor out of possession. The reason was because he didn't prepare himself."
Ten Hag also claimed promises made by United's owners went unfulfilled before he was sacked in 2024, shortly after signing a new contract.
Although United won the FA Cup just months earlier with a surprise final victory against Manchester City, Ten Hag was axed with the team languishing in 14th place in the Premier League.
The Dutchman blamed the United hierarchy of some of his problems, saying he was left humiliated when Scotland midfielder Scott McTominay was sold to Napoli without his consent.
Ten Hag also said he wanted to sign Harry Kane, Declan Rice and Frenkie de Jong during his spell at United.
"They promised me loyalty, they promised me backing, they promised communication, that we get aligned. We spoke about the issues. But the promises, they didn't keep," he said.
"I said, 'No selling Scott McTominay'. And in the end they sold him. I got, of course, very embarrassed and disappointed." — AFP
02b5e9a4ed9409e9: SAN FRANCISCO: Anthropic reported a net loss of more than US$80 billion in the first half of the year and signalled it could spend as much as US$750 billion in the coming years to secure more computing capacity, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday.

The loss, up from US$13 billion a year earlier, was driven by $US72 billion in accounting charges tied to changes in the value of financial instruments Anthropic issued to raise money, the report said, citing a draft prospectus for its IPO.
The figures show the hefty costs of the AI race even as investors look harder at whether the money companies are pouring into chips and data centres will pay off.

Anthropic's revenue jumped to US$16.3 billion in the six months ended June 30 from US$1.1 billion a year ago, while AI infrastructure spending nearly quadrupled to almost US$9 billion, the Journal said.
Anthropic did not respond to a request for comment and Reuters could not immediately verify the report.
Reuters reported first in September that Anthropic posted a net loss of US$42 billion ‌in 2025, as part of a series of exclusives from its IPO prospectus.
The company has benefited from the popularity of Claude Code, its coding assistant that developers use to write software and build apps.

But some current investors and prospective investors who attended Anthropic's investor day last week are weighing a lower valuation ‌for the AI company after its latest financial disclosures, four people familiar with the matter had told Reuters.

The investors who attended the event in San Francisco discussed a valuation of around US$1.5 trillion, three of the people had said, a significant step down from the roughly US$2 trillion valuation previously expected for the November share sale.
Anthropic told investors at the meeting that its third-quarter revenue jumped ​45% to US$16.8 billion from the previous quarter, and that it was profitable on an adjusted basis during the quarter.

A cooler reception for Anthropic's IPO could weigh on the wider AI market, whose near-term prospects investors see as hinging largely on the share sale's success, ahead of rival OpenAI's potential listing next year.
463549bb3cc6ed70: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Wednesday, supported by strong domestic economic data that strengthened expectations of a possible normalisation of the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR).
At 8am, the ringgit strengthened to 4.0795/4.0850 against the greenback from Tuesday’s close of 4.0805/4.0845.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Afzanizam Rashid said robust economic indicators, particularly export growth and gross domestic product (GDP) expansion, provide support for the local currency.

“Strong data points for the Malaysian economy have raised the odds of a possible OPR normalisation. The latest trade data showed exports jumped 54.5% in September, while GDP grew 5.3% in the third quarter of 2026, exceeding consensus forecasts,” he said.

Afzanizam added that easing expectations of a US interest rate hike at the Federal Reserve’s October meeting contributed to a 0.27% fall in the US Dollar Index (DXY) to 101.707 points, further supporting the ringgit.
At the opening, the ringgit traded mostly lower against a basket of major currencies.

It gained versus the Japanese yen to 2.5772/2.5809 from 2.5803/2.5830 at Tuesday’s close, but fell against the British pound to 5.4551/5.4625 from 5.4475/5.4528 and edged down against the euro to 4.5796/4.5858 from 4.5771/4.5816.
The ringgit performed mixed against its Asean peers.
It traded marginally higher versus the Indonesian rupiah at 226.7/227.1 from 226.8/227.1, and gained slightly against the Philippine peso to 6.46/6.48 from 6.47/6.48.
The local currency was lower against the Thai baht to 12.1341/12.1577 from 12.1241/12.1411 at yesterday’s close and depreciated versus the Singapore dollar to 3.1918/3.1964 from 3.1914/3.1950.
